system.description: Those Scout Ninja who choose to become Defensive Scouts train to bolster those around them. They can inspire their allies with renewed vigor, lifting them to new heights, while simultaneously protecting them from harm.

The Scout-Nin who choose to become Arbiters focus on enhancing their allies, utilizing their skills beyond what most shinobi could only dream of doing, and enabling their team to perform feats of amazing prowess with just a bit of Arbitration.

The Scout-Nin who choose to become a Phantom becomes a ghost who fades in and out of sight, acting as a specter who is virtually impossible to touch or find. A master of Stealth and expert in assassination, using your ghostly Ninjutsu and Genjutsu to execute your objectives with little to no opposition.

Those Scout Ninja who choose to become Tactical Specialists employ martial techniques passed down through generations. To a Tactical Specialist, combat is an academic field, sometimes including subjects beyond battle such as weaponsmith or armor craft. Not every scout absorbs the lessons of history, theory, and artistry that are reflected in the Tactical Specialty, but those who do are well-rounded fighters of great skill and knowledge.
The Ninjutsu Specialist who chooses to become a Storm Terror becomes a ruthless natural disaster and unmatched collateral destruction when using Wind Release Ninjutsu.

The Scout-Nin who choose to become a Void Heart have found a way to become true to themselves and those around them, by directly and consciously accessing their Id, Ego and Superego. By accepting who they truly are, they have gained the ability to manifest the best version of themselves and become a Shinobi beyond what they could have originally dreamed of.

The Ninjutsu Specialist who chooses to become a Tsunami embodies the force of such an event. Unphased by the power of the sea and all-encompassing just like an ocean when using Water Release Ninjutsu.
The Ninjutsu Specialist who chooses to become a Lightning Breaker, becomes an unmatched force of unstoppable power greater than that of a Lightning storm when using Lightning Release Ninjutsu.

The Scout-Nin who choose to become Elementalist learn to wield a Nature Release and have it constantly flowing through their chakra coils, just beneath the surface. Making their element stronger and themselves sturdier against it.

Limited Casting. The Bunshin can cast 1 Jutsu from its casters known list after which, it is dispelled. This increases to 2 at 10th and 3 at 17th level. Bunshins can only make one attack with a jutsu per casting, regardless of the number of attacks a jutsu asks for and they can maintain concentration on jutsu they cast until the beginning of your next turn, after which they lose concentration.

Placement. Bunshin you summon must be in a space within 60 feet of you.

Basic Tools. The Bunshin has a basic version of one weapon its summoner has void of any weapon seals. It uses this weapon (If any) as part of its Bunshin strike. Its Bunshin Strike shares the range of this weapon. If no weapon, then it strike unarmed.

Gang Up. When more than one Bunshin is attacking or targeting the same target, you do not make multiple attacks and the target does not make multiple saving throws, instead consolidate their attacks into a single attack roll or saving throw. Increase Bunshin Strike’s or Bunshins Cast damage by +4 for each Bunshin beyond the first.

Hiding In Plain Sight. Bunshin are indiscernible from their summoner, so much so, that not even chakra sight can tell them apart. When one or more Bunshin are active, hostile creatures must perform the Search action at disadvantage vs the Summoners Stealth DC to determine that the Bunshins are clones.

Bunshins Cast. The Bunshin casts a jutsu on its summoners known list of C-Rank or lower that doesn’t have the Fuinjutsu or Combination keyword using the casters statistics to determine its attack bonus or save DC. If the jutsu deals damage, it deals an amount of damage equal to the rank the jutsu is cast at. (D-Rank: 2d6, C-Rank: 3d6, B-Rank: 4d6, A-Rank: 5d6, S-Rank: 6d6).

Those Scout-Nin that choose to become Cloning specialist employ superior numbers as their primary method of combat. They hone this skill through repeated use of their Clones in different situations allowing them to becomes masters of duplicative combat. Not every scout has the ability to use Clones the way a Cloning Scout can and it shows through their tactics and abilities available to them.

The Ninjutsu Specialist who chose this Tradition to become a Summoner, walk the path closest to Sage hood. Those who walk this path are best known for having a wide arrangement of jutsu learned from the sage creatures themselves.
The Ninjutsu Specialist who becomes a Stone Crusher, becomes an unwavering force of strength, tenacity and mountain like toughness when using Earth Release Ninjutsu.

The Scout-Nin who choose to become Pathfinder Scouts use extreme speed to nearly teleport around the battlefield. They use their extreme speed to protect their allies and maneuver them more effectively during battle.

Taijutsu Specialists who follow the path of Talented Genius are the prodigies of their generation. Defined by clarity of thought, precise execution, and an innate understanding of combat, they turn even the simplest movement into a display of mastery. While others strain to refine their form, these shinobi seem to flow effortlessly from stance to strike, their technique honed to a standard that borders on perfection.

Taijutsu specialists who blend their style with the Art of disturbance have a level of trickery mixed into their fighting. They focus on overwhelming their enemies with a flurry of attacks from multiple angles at once. You can break, the momentum of even the most focused fighters.

Elemental Cloak

Fortitude Amp

Taijutsu you cast deal its nature releases associated damage type and your chosen nature release grants your cloak different benefits.

Earth Release: You gain +4 DR. This DR cannot be reduced by any means. When you reach 10th, you gain 30 feet of tremor sense. Increase DR to +6 at 17th level.

Wind Release: You gain a +1 Bonus to AC, and damage you deal with Taijutsu penetrates 2 of a creatures DR. When you reach 10th level, you gain immunity to the Grappled and Restrained conditions. Finally, when you reach 17th level, your bonuses becomes +2 to AC and penetrates 4 DR.

Fire Release: You gain a rank of Mastery to [Unarmed Damage]. This becomes two ranks of Mastery at 10th and three ranks at 17th level.

Water Release: Your unarmed attacks gain the Reach 1 and Trip weapon properties. Beginning at 10th level the first time each turn you deal [Unarmed Damage] to a creature you can move them up to 10 feet in any direction of your choice. Finally, at 17th level, level creatures cannot gain jutsu based bonuses to their saving throws vs Taijutsu you cast.

Lightning Release: Your unarmed and Taijutsu attacks gain a +1 bonus to their critical threat range and a +10 to speed. Beginning at 10th level, when you score a critical with an unarmed attack, you may add 1 unarmed damage die to the result. Finally, at 17th level, [Unarmed Damage] you deal cannot have its damage intercepted, always affecting its original target.

The Taijutsu specialist who Blend their style with Ninjutsu open up a world of unpredictability and technique. They have found ways to further augment their body beyond simple Taijutsu, but instead coating their body in a given Nature Releases and magnifying their strength and greatly increasing their potential.

Taijutsu Specialists who take specialize in multiple stances, are known as Stancers. They are style collectors. They analyze every opponent and every clan for an opportunity to learn something more. They are able to weave in multiple stances into one another so quickly that an enemy cannot predict the rhythm. Their body shifts instinctively from one stance to the next in the blink of an eye.
The Ninjutsu Specialist who chooses to become a Blaze Walker, becomes a primal engine of destruction when using Fire Release Ninjutsu.

A Hyūga takes their fighting stance, ready for the assault from the surrounding undead summons from the Dark shinobi standing just on the other side of the ridge, the Hyūga leaps from undead to undead, striking them each with unmatched precision taking them down one by one with 1 or two precise strikes.

Taijutsu Specialist

A clanless girl in the heat of battle creates an unorthodox stance, and readies for her training session. Her team assaults her as she parries, dodges and counters each one with a graceful swing of her arms and legs as she then follows each one with a powerful strike knocking each training member back.

These shinobi, different as they might be, are connected by one common factor, they are masters in the field of Taijutsu. While others are able to use Taijutsu techniques they learn with some level of mastery, the Taijutsu Specialists are the absolute masters of unarmed combat and technique. They are able to take the concepts of the Taijutsu they have and accelerate it to new heights and unmatched levels.

Character Inspirations

When designing this class, it was built with the intent to allow players to utilize different types of Taijutsu and stances, allowing for a variety of fighting styles as shown in the Naruto series and other Manga series. Players would be able to match or exceed their allies in combat, close range and even close distance better than most other classes are able. The characters this class is pulling inspiration from are as follows: Rock Lee, Might Guy, Neji Hyūga, Hinata Hyūga, and Killer B

Creating A Taijutsu Specialist

When creating a Taijutsu Specialist consider a few things about the character on a personal level? Do they use Taijutsu as a way to push pass their weaknesses and surpass their rivals? Do they use Taijutsu as a way to give themselves discipline and teach themselves patience?

What made the character so bound to learning so many varied and useful Taijutsu techniques and what drives them to learn more? Did they train under another very skilled Shinobi? Or did they become enamored by the people around them and want to emulate their skills and techniques?

Quick Build

You can make a Taijutsu Specialist quickly by following these suggestions. First, put your highest ability score in Strength or Dexterity, followed by Constitution. Second, choose the Hyūga, Sarutobi, Inuzuka, Uchiha or Non-Clan, Clans.

Those Scout-Ninja who choose to become Assault Specialists focus on the development of raw physical power honed to deadly perfection. Assault Specialist Scouts combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows.

An Uzumaki lies in wait as his target enters the brothel, he performs the transformation technique to turn into one of the many women within the building he’s seen in the past few days.

A Sarutobi in the heat of battle weaves together a great wave of water blowing some enemies away, when some leap over the wave avoiding it, the Sarutobi follows up with a powerful Genjutsu stunning the airborne shinobi as they come crashing down into the water.

A Nara gets into a close combat battle with an enemy, and holds his own while preparing to capture his enemy within the Shadow possession technique.

These shinobi, different as they might be, are connected by one common factor, they are Jack of all trades. While others are specialists of some sort in one form or another, a scout-nin is someone who by definition is able to complete most tasks or fill most roles in a team with little trouble. Scout-Nin are able to draw out their latent abilities in most fields while others cannot.

Character Inspirations

When designing this class, it was built with the intent to allow players to take on the role of a generalist, someone who may not specialize in any particular field such as ninjutsu, Genjutsu or Taijutsu. But someone who can use them all to a varying degree and find success. While other classes can use all 3 forms of jutsu, this class is designed with the ability to enhance them on a case-by-case basis using Superiority dice if needed. Characters whom this class was designed after are as follows; Kid Naruto Uzumaki, Kid Sasuke Uchiha, Kid Sakura Haruno, Kid Kakashi Hatake and Kid Obito Uchiha.

Creating A Scout-Nin

When creating a Scout-Nin consider a few things about the character when they are on a team with others. Do they fill in any gaps or do they support others in their endeavors enhancing that particular field their allies are specializing in. Do they use their techniques as an answer to the weaknesses of the team? What made the character so bound to learning so many varied techniques and how do they plan on using them in the field? Did they train under another very skilled Shinobi? Or did they become enamored by the people around them and want to emulate their skills and techniques leaving nothing to chance?

Quick Build

You can make a Scout-Nin quickly by following these suggestions. First, put your highest ability score in either Strength, Intelligence, or Wisdom followed by Constitution. Second, choose any clan that you find the most appealing, this class is flexible enough to support them.

A clanless boy quickly weaves hand seals and places his hands onto a large chakra seal, igniting the seals as the door begins to open. The boy walks through the open doors and after weaving a few seals with one hand he conjures orbs of fire creating light for him to see.

An Uzumaki in the heat of battle creates a single hand seal and conjures 10 Shadow Clones as they all surround a single enemy. The Clones and the Uzumaki all weave hand seals and each create a super dense blade of wind chakra that all converge on their target leaving him no room to dodge or evade.

These shinobi, different as they might be, are connected by one common factor, they are masters in the field of Ninjutsu. While others are able to use the techniques, they learn with some level of mastery, the Ninjutsu Specialists are able to draw out the true essence of the Ninjutsu arts. They are able to take the concepts of the Ninjutsu they have and accelerate it to new heights and unmatched levels.

Character Inspirations

When designing this class, it was built with the intent to allow players to utilize ninjutsu in a variety of ways and allows for a mastery of the techniques they have that surpass others. Players would be able to have a larger variety of ninjutsu at their disposal and in some cases have access to different forms of ninjutsu before others such as Elemental ninjutsu. Players should be able to exemplify characters who embody this style of rapid fire ninjutsu such as: Kakashi Hatake, Sasuke Uchiha, Orochimaru, Hiruzen Sarutobi (3rd Hokage), Hashirama Senju, Tobirama Senju, Jiraiya and Madara Uchiha.

Creating A Ninjutsu Specialist

When creating a Ninjutsu-Specialist consider a few things about the character on a personal level? Think of Ninjutsu as a tool? Do they use ninjutsu as a ring of keys, a way through every door or a sledge hammer, a way to pass through any obstacle? What made the character so bound to learning so many powerful ninjutsu and what drives them to learn more? Did they train under another very skilled Shinobi? Or did they become enamored by the people around them and want to emulate their skills and techniques?

Quick Build

You can make a Ninjutsu Specialist quickly by following these suggestions. First, put your highest ability score in Intelligence, followed by Constitution or Dexterity. Second, choose the Sarutobi, Uchiha, Uzumaki or Non-Clan, Clans.

Taijutsu Specialists who blend their style with the passionate flame exude a level of tenacity unmatched by most in the world of Taijutsu. This group of martial artists are exemplified by green jumpsuits, weighted clothing, and very eccentric haircuts. While this group is mostly associated with the 8-Inner Gates, that technique is formally forbidden from use, and so to avoid having to tap into that potentially fatal reserve of power, they focus on ensuring that their bodies are at the peak of human skill and conditioning beyond all doubts.

Combo Extender. This Taijutsu is treated as a one with the Combo keyword. Also, until the end of your next turn, you can cast one Taijutsu with the Combo keyword, using either an Action or Bonus action, ignoring its listed casting time.

Also, at 3rd level, you become the leader your team needs in times of strife and conflict. Someone who can lead the team to victory no matter the odds. When you complete a rest, you select a number of creatures other than yourself, equal to your proficiency bonus that you designate as your Squad-Mate(s), sometimes simply referred to as Squad.

You and your Squad gain the following benefits when in combat:

When initiative is rolled, you and your Squad gain a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Charisma Modifier.

Once per turn, when you would take the Attack Action, in place of one of your attacks, you can select one member of your Squad who can see or hear you and Command them. They can do one of the following of their choice;

Make a weapon attack.

Cast a Jutsu of D-Rank or lower that requires an attack roll. This increases to C-Rank at 10th level and B-Rank at 17th.

Perform a Skill-based Action. You regain 1 superiority die.

Take the Dodge action

Take the Disengage action and move up to half their speed. You regain 1 superiority die.

When a Squad-Mate makes an attack of any type, you can spend a Superiority die and your Reaction, to make a weapon attack against the same target if you can. On a hit, you add your Superiority dies result to both your own and the triggering allies damage rolls.

When emboldened in this way, you generate a zone of terror around no more than one affected creature until the end of your next turn. This zone is called a Storm Zone and radiates outward in a 60-foot radius, centered on the select creature. Hostile creatures in this zone cannot benefit from cover, concealment or Invisibility, their ranged attacks are made at disadvantage, and Jutsu they cast with the Barrier keyword are summoned with half of their listed or rolled hit points.

Beginning at 10th level, your Bunshin evolve from distractions to elemental instruments of warfare, tuned to react, retaliate, and reshape the flow of battle at your command. First, increase the number of Bunshin you can have active to a maximum of 6.

Second, If a Ninjutsu you have that has the clone keyword also has a nature release keyword, when you summon a Bunshin, they can gain a specialized bonus based on the keyword you have access to. A Bunshin can only benefit from one keyword bonus at a time and you can only have up to two different keywords active at once, regardless of the number of Bunshin you have.

Earth Release. Your Bunshins hit points become 10, instead of 1. Additionally, they gain 10 DR and 10 temporary hit points for the duration of their life. At the beginning of each of your turns, they regain 10 temporary hit points.

Fire Release. Your Bunshins are walking bombs. When they fall to 0 hit points, they detonate forcing all creatures within 10 feet of them must make a Dexterity saving throw vs your Ninjutsu save DC, taking 6d6 fire damage on a failed save. A creature can only make a saving tactical, Phantom or hrow vs this effect twice per turn..

Water Release. Your Bunshins take no damage if they pass a saving throw. Additionally, they can use your Ninjutsu attack bonus in place of their saving throw bonus.

Lightning Release. Your Bunshins are extremely potent. When they deal damage, they use d8’s in instead of d6’s.

system.description:
Beginning at 7th level, you have found a jutsu that you specialize in better than anyone else who may have come before. Select one Jutsu you know of B-Rank or Lower. The chosen jutsu becomes known as your Signature Jutsu, gaining one of the following Signature Modification of your choice when casting the chosen Jutsu and when cast, it can count as your Primary jutsu regardless of its casting discipline keyword. You may switch which jutsu this feature affects whenever you would complete a Full-Rest. You can select a second Signature effect, which the chosen Jutsu gains the benefits of as well, at 15th level.

Signature Modification - Power

When you use your chosen jutsu, your Jutsu ignores resistance to its damage and treats immunity to its damage as resistance.

If you are gaining the benefit of the Warfare generalization, you add your Jutsu’s ability modifier to the damage dealt.

If you are gaining the benefit of the Seize generalization, you can cast your chosen jutsu as a Bonus Action, in place of an Action. You cannot cast your Chosen jutsu as an Action if you do. If you already cast your chosen jutsu as an Action, you cannot cast it as a Bonus action using this ability.

Signature Modification - Ramping

When you upcast your chosen jutsu, increase the number of damage or healing dice it rolls by +1.

If you are gaining the benefit of the Seize generalization, and a creature casts a Jutsu as a reaction to something you do, they increase the cost of that jutsu by an amount equal to your level.

If you are gaining the benefit of the Tactics generalization, if your jutsu requires an attack, you can use one skill-based action that requires an Action or Bonus Action, as part of the attack.

Signature Modification - Refinement

When you would cast your chosen jutsu, reduce the cost of the chosen jutsu by an amount equal to its rank. (D-Rank: 1, C-Rank: 2, B-Rank: 3, A-Rank: 4, S-Rank: 5).

If you are gaining the benefit of the Tactics generalization, if the jutsu you cast requires you to make a check, you gain a +1d4 bonus to the result.

If you are gaining the benefit of the Warfare generalization, you can use two Maneuvers per turn, even using them both as part of your chosen jutsu’s casting.

If the creature is unwilling, they must make on a Charisma saving throw against your Ninjutsu (or Taijutsu) save DC. On a failed save they swap places with you. Once per turn, when you would cast a jutsu with the Wind Release keyword or make a Ninjutsu attack using a weapon with the Evocation property, you build Pressure. You can maintain up to 3 Pressure at a time and they last for 1 minute or until spent. For every Pressure you begin your turn with you gain +2 temporary hit points as your swirling wind release chakra protects you. You can spend Pressure in the following ways. If an ability requires a saving throw, you use your Ninjutsu save DC.

Gale Burst. As part of casting a Ninjutsu with the wind release keyword or make a Ninjutsu attack using a weapon with the Evocation property, you can spend 1 Pressure to force all creatures within 10 feet of you to make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, they are pushed 10 feet away from you and are knocked prone.

Sharpening. Once per turn, as part of casting a Ninjutsu with the wind release keyword or make a Ninjutsu attack using a weapon with the Evocation property that deals damage, you can spend 1 Pressure to increase the lethality of the jutsu cast, dealing +1 Wind damage for every damage dice rolled, up to a maximum of +10.

Dragwind. As part of the casting a Ninjutsu with the wind release keyword that affects an area, you can spend 1 Pressure to increase the size of the affected area by +5 feet. This increases to +10 feet at 10th and +15 at 18th levels.

You push your chakra network to its limits outputting more than humanly possible.

15th Level. While in the Crash state, you can use one Molding at no Focus cost, once every other turn.

Crash Evolution

Your thrashing chakra can bypass constructs and structures as if they were formed of less tough stuff.

9th Level. While in the Crash state, structures and constructs that would intercept your Ninjutsu attacks now allows half of your damage to affect its intended target if the attack roll would have hit the original target.

15th Level. While in the Crash state, Ninjutsu you cast that would force a saving throw but have a structure or constructs intercepting it still forces creatures that would be in the affected areas range to make a saving throw. On a failed save the affected creatures take half damage and the structure takes the full damage. On a success, throw only the structure takes damage.

Harmony

Flow Evolution

Your chakra harmonizes with your allies.

9th Level. While in the Flow state, when an allied creature within 30 feet casts a Jutsu you can spend your reaction to apply your Save DC bonus to their Jutsu.

15th Level. While in the Flow state, when an allied creature within 30 feet makes a saving throw against a jutsu you can spend 1 Focus to apply your Save DC bonus to their saving throw result.

Circuit

Flow Evolution

You maintain a clean chakra flow, reducing waste and internal friction.

9th Level. While in the Flow state, Ninjutsu you cast that require concentration cost 0 chakra to concentrate on the first time you maintain it, costing its normal amount every time you maintain it thereafter.

15th Level. While in the Flow state, you gain immunity to hostile effects that would increase the cost of jutsu you cast.

Union

Neutral Evolution

You have an even balance of synergy between Crash and Flow.

9th Level. Once per turn, at the start of your turn, you can swap your state without spending a Bonus action.

15th Level. Once per turn, when you swap your state, you regain 1 Focus.

system.description:
Starting at 3rd level, you learn a special Fuinjutsu technique to infuse your inner most Id, Ego and Superego into a mask of your creation and description, creating a duplicate chakra construct known as a Void Soul, a manifestation of your true self, that you can call upon for support. Your Void Soul when summoned looks like how you wish yourself to be otherwise called your ideal self with the caveat of always wearing the custom mask and being unable to take it off. Your Void Soul can be summoned as a bonus action and occupies your space alongside you. It is visible to all creatures.

Once summoned, you can command it by spending your Bonus Actions. Your Void soul uses the Statistics in the Void Soul stat block at the end of this class section; Your Void soul has the following rules.

Your Void Soul knows a number of Jutsu known equal to your proficiency bonus.

Your Void Soul can only learn jutsu which you could normally qualify for (Keywords, Hijutsu, etc.), plus one keyword that you don’t have access to (Any one nature release or medical keyword).

You can switch your Void Soul’s Jutsu known when you would gain a level.

It uses its own ability scores for the purpose of qualifying for jutsu. These jutsu are added to your known jutsu list, but you cannot cast them, only your void soul can.

Movement speed is equal to yours. If you would end your turn more than 60 feet away from your Void Soul, it is resummoned in your space.

Uses your Chakra when casting its Jutsu.

If your Void Soul would take damage, you lose hit points equal to the damage taken.

Your Void Soul has your same saving throw proficiencies.

If you and Void Soul would make a saving throw against the same effect, you only make one save suffering the effects only once.

If the Void soul would take damage, you do not need to make a concentration check.

You can dismiss your Void Soul as a bonus action on your turn or when you fall unconscious.

Finally, your Void Soul does not have Ability scores like a normal creature, but instead only Ability Modifiers. You may distribute the following Ability modifiers and apply it to your Void Soul giving each modifier to a chosen ability once (+4, +3, +2, +2, +1, +0).

Starting at 6th level, in place of an attack made as part of your attack action or as a Bonus Action, you may make a Maintain Focus check vs a creature you can see within 60 feet Constitution Save DC. Natural Perception. You become aware of the nature releases the target has access to.

Also at 3rd Level, you learn to compress your phantasmic chakra for bursts of ghastly power known as your Phantasmic Flame. In order to fuel your Phantasmic Flame, you must first build up and spend Ghostfire.

Ghostfire. Once per turn, when you benefit from the Follow Up status or perform a Skill based Action, you gain 1 Ghostfire (Max 3), of which last for 1 minute. Ghostfire is represented as soft blue embers or motes of illusory flame that manifest themselves in any way of your description. You can spend Ghost fire when a feature requires it. You begin with the following Phantasmic Flame abilities.

Phantasm’s Grip. When you take the attack action or cast a jutsu that requires an attack, you can spend 1 Ghostfire, giving the attack/jutsu the Genjutsu keyword for the purposes of interacting with class features. The triggering attack, shifts it into one that strikes the mind or chakra coils. The attacks damage type becomes psychic or chakra damage (your choice). If the jutsu or maneuver used would inflict a condition, all ranks of the condition that would be inflicted is replaced with Concussed. If the attack is made as part of the attack action, then the affected creature must make a Wisdom saving throw vs your Ninjutsu (or Genjutsu) save DC, gaining 1 rank of Concussed on a failed save. Regardless, If the attack result is 5 or higher than the targets AC, you regain 1 Superiority die.

Ghost Walk. When you would interact with or walk into a solid structure, you gain an incorporeal form, capable of phasing through solid matter like a ghost. As part of movement on your turn, you can spend 1 Ghostfire to become incorporeal until the end of your current turn. While incorporeal you can move through objects and walls that are not made by jutsu or reinforced with chakra. If you end your movement inside an object or structure, your body is shunted out of it, into the closest space that can hold you, taking 10 necrotic damage for every 5 feet you are forced through while being pushed out. Damage taken in this way cannot be resisted, reduced or ignored by any means.

1 Damage Die. By forgoing 1 damage dice, all Linked creatures suffer a surge of electricity through their body, reducing their speed by half.

Starting at 6th Level, through relentless discipline and a lifetime of unconventional conditioning, you have forged your body into a weapon. But what others don’t know, is that everything you’ve done until now, has been you restrained by self-imposed limiters. You now have the confidence to unleash those. You have been using the following training implements and can utilize them in combat. Select one of the following training implements, gaining it. You may select a second one at 14th level.

Binding Hand Wraps. Special weighted chakra enhanced wraps that you use to band your hands, arms, legs or feet during training. These wraps are treated as a martial weapon, that you are proficient in with the following traits; Light, Disarm, Reach 1, Grapple, Unarmed, Hidden. If you would perform a Taijutsu Finisher against a creature grappled by these hand wraps, you can select a number of damage die rolled, up to half of your proficiency bonus, and treat them as the maximum value.

Training Weights. You have been training under the strain of 500lb weighted gear, forcing your body to move with explosive potential when freed from its duress. As a bonus action you may drop your weights, removing them for 1 minute. While unweighted, your movement speed increases by +20 feet and the first attack you make each turn creates an afterimage from the sheer speed at which you strike. When you make a melee unarmed or Taijutsu attack, you may immediately make an unarmed attack. This attack does not add your ability modifier to damage. After one minute, your muscle cramp up and tire, requiring you to re-weight them for at least 10 minute before unweighting them again.

Specialized Training Kit. You carry a unique set of training tools that you’ve learned to use via muscle memory. You have proficiency in this kit. You may select two toolkits found in Chapter 5: Equipment. Your specialized Training kit counts as both of the selected toolkits and has 5 charges to utilize per rest. It grows in usefulness as you grow in level, being treated as Greater kits at 10th level, and Superior kits at 14th level.

Beginning at 3rd level you learn maneuvers that capitalize on your ability to divide and conquer with your ability to multiply yourself which are fueled by your Superiority Die.

You learn two maneuvers of your choice, which are detailed in the Cloning Maneuvers Section at the end of this class. You earn more at higher levels as shown in the Maneuvers Known Column of the Scout-Nin Class table. Maneuvers normally enhance your unarmed or Weapon attacks or jutsu you cast in some way. You can use one maneuver per turn as part of an unarmed or weapon attack made with the Attack Action or as part of a Bonus Action attack or as part of a jutsu’s casting. You add the Shadow Clone Technique Ninjutsu to your known jutsu list and can cast it as a Bonus Action. You can also learn any Ninjutsu with the Clone keyword, ignoring any nature release keyword requirements. When you summon a clone, you can choose to instead summon a Bunshin, using the Bunshin stat block instead of the cast jutsu’s clone. You can have up to 4 Bunshins active at once, and so long as you have Bunshins active, you cannot summon or have clones summoned as a result of jutsu with the Clone keyword active. Bunshins last for 1 minute in combat or 1 hour outside of combat. Bunshins can exist up to 1 mile away from you, but if they would enter combat in any way, they are immediately dispelled. When a Bunshin is dispelled, you gain all the information that Bunshin had prior to being dispelled. You can command Bunshins in the following ways;

Where I say. Once per turn, at no action cost, you can command all active Bunshin to move into a space of your choice within their movement speeds range.

Clone Strike. Once per turn, when you would take the Attack Action, in place of one of your attacks, you can command one or more of your Bunshin to perform a Bunshin Strike or Bunshin Cast.

Split Focus. Once per turn, as a Bonus action, you can command one of your Bunshin to perform a Skill based action or the Help action for one of your allies.

A sage creature that is Bonded with you is different from all the rest, as they grow alongside you, benefiting from the following. You can only have one Bonded creature and this cannot be changed, except by GM intervention.

They are always summoned at the highest rank possible, but at half the chakra cost. They share your level, using it level in place of their own for calculating their AC and Hit points.

When you complete a rest, your Bonded creature regains half of their maximum hit points and Jutsu slots.

Your Bonded creature has one of its Tribes Roles, called their Primary Role plus one additional Role of your choice found in Jiraiya’s Jutsu, Summoning Jutsu Section.

Once per turn, when you deal unarmed damage to a hostile creature as a result of an attack or a Taijutsu you cast, you gain 1 Momentum (Max 4) and last for 1 minute.

Momentum is represented as your ability to exchange your own combat momentum in order to interrupt your nemesis. You can spend momentum you have on the following abilities.

Blitzing Momentum. By spending 1 Momentum on your turn, you increase your movement speed by +10 feet and until the beginning of your next turn, when you take a Reaction, you can move 10 feet as part of the reaction. If your reaction would already grant you movement as part of it, you increase the distance of that movement by +10 feet.

Surging Momentum. Once per turn, by spending 2 Momentum on your turn, you gain an additional Bonus action, which can only be used to cast a Taijutsu of D-Rank or lower. This becomes C-Rank at 10th level and B-Rank at 17th level. This additional bonus action lasts until the end of current turn. If it is not used, it is lost.

Disturbing Momentum. Once per turn, by spending 2 Momentum on a hostile creatures turn, you gain an additional Reaction, which can only be used to cast a Taijutsu or use a Martial Technique. This additional reaction lasts until the end of the current turn. If it is not used, it is lost.

Starting at 5th Level, you learn how to relax your chakra pathway system, allowing you to regain your composure in a swift and more effective manner than most others.

When you complete a short rest, if you have less than half of your maximum Focus, you set your Focus to half of its maximum value.

Finally, at 1st Level, your training emphasizes adaptability over raw reflexes. Whether it's gauging enemy intent, reacting with raw physicality, or sensing fluctuations in chakra, you can leverage specialized knowledge to seize the initiative. When you would roll Initiative, you can choose to substitute your Initiative bonus with one of the following skills, based on the circumstances of the encounter. If the GM determines that your declared substitution is not relevant to the encounter’s opening situation, they may require you to roll Initiative instead

Athletics. You can substitute your initiative for an Athletics check if prior to combat breaking out you were doing something physically demanding or athletic in nature.

Ninshou. You can substitute your initiative for a Ninshou check if prior to combat, you could sense the chakra of a hostile creature or are concentrating on a Ninjutsu at the time of combat being initiated.

Illusion. You can substitute your initiative for an Illusion check if prior to combat you were investigating a Genjutsu, concentrating on a Genjutsu or are under the effects of a Genjutsu at the time of combat being initiated.

Insight. You can substitute your initiative for an insight check if you are aware of the emotional or intents of the creatures you are initiating combat with or if you are aware their current attitude towards you is Hostile prior to combat being initiated.

All it takes is a single strike to completely break an enemies flow, stopping them in their tracks and bringing them to their knees. When you use this technique, they must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they are Flow Broken. Once you use this Martial Technique you cannot do so again until the end of your next turn.

system.description:
Starting, at 3rd level, your brutish nature in combat has compelled you to learn to overcome any and every one you consider your rival. This drive has pushed you to become a brutal combatant capable of overwhelming whoever is your enemy with simple but effective tactics.

When initiative is rolled, you may select one creature you can see. This creature is marked as your Combat Rival. Creatures marked as your Combat Rival cannot be changed and remain so until combat ends or either you or they reach 0 hit points, whichever occurs first. When a Combat Rival reached 0 hit points, you may immediately select a new Combat Rival so long as you are still in initiative. While you have a Combat Rival you can use the following abilities.

Relentless Durability. Once per turn, when you take damage you can spend 1 Superiority Die, gaining temporary hit points equal to the result. This increases to twice the result at 10th level and three times the result at 17th level. These Temporary hit points last until the end of the current turn.

Relentless Aggression. Once per turn, when score a hit against your Combat Rival on your turn with an attack as a result of the Attack action, you can perform one of the following Skill Based Actions; Trip, Grapple, Shove or Disarm using your attack result in place of your skill check.

Relentless Pursuit. When your Combat Rival would move further than 5 feet away from you at the conclusion of their movement, you can spend your reaction to move up to your full speed closer to them. If you end your movement in range, you can make an unarmed or weapon attack, adding your Superiority Die to the damage result.

Relentless Progress. The first time each turn you score a hit against your Combat Rival with an attack whose result is 5 or higher than their AC, or they fail a saving throw by 5 or more as a result of a jutsu you cast, you regain 1 Superiority Die.

activities.label: Relentless Durability
activities.text: When you take damage.

system.description: In place of an attack made as a result of the attack action, you can spend 1 Martial Die to instead strike a pressure point meant to induce sleep. If the target creature is an Elite or Solo adversary or they are of a higher level than you, they are immune to this technique. Roll your Martial Die, multiplying the result by 10. If the final value is more than or equal to the targets current hit points you knock them unconscious for the next 10 minutes. The creature is awoken if moved, they take damage, or another creature uses its action to wake it. A creature becomes immune to this technique for 8 hours after it is used against them regardless if it succeeded or not.

If you take the Attack action using a Kunai, Shuriken or Senbon, you can attack three times, instead of twice, whenever you attack with those weapons.

Finally, the following explosive tools gain a d4 ammunition die instead of a set number of charges/uses, so long as they are of base quality; Chili Pepper Bombs, Paper Bombs, Flash Tags, and Smoke Bombs.

Scout-Nin Keyword: Specialized

When you would cast a Jutsu that affects an area that includes your Combat Rival, you can spend a superiority die. When you do, the jutsu cast loses its area of effect size, and now only affects your Combat Rival. When your combat rival makes their saving throw, they make it at disadvantage.

When you choose this style starting at 3rd level, you have focused your effort on harnessing your innate element. If you have access to one or more nature releases already, select one. It becomes your chosen nature release that this and other feature from this subclass references.

If you do not have access to one, you may select one (Earth, Wind, Fire, Water, or Lightning Release). You gain the ability to learn and cast jutsu with the corresponding keyword.

Taijutsu you cast gains the chosen nature release keyword, if they don’t have one already.

By spending 1 Martial Dice, as a Bonus Action, you enhance your body with the Chakra of your chosen Nature release putting you into your Elemental Cloak state for the next minute or until you spend a bonus action to end it early. Once you enter this state, you cannot do so again until you spend at least 10 minutes of uninterrupted meditating.

Elemental Finisher

Taijutsu you cast with the Finisher keyword that are changed to become an Elemental Finisher gains the effects of the corresponding nature release.

Earth Release: You strike the ground creating a massive tectonic shift. All creatures in a 20-foot radius, centering on a point of the space you are occupying must make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (your choice). On a failed save, they take your [Unarmed Damage] + earth damage equal to the rank of the Jutsu cast, are knocked prone, and you create an area of difficult terrain equal to the rank the jutsu cast. Hostiles who attempt to move through this terrain must also pass a Perception check vs your Save DC or take earth damage equal to half of the rank the Jutsu was cast, taking none on a successful save. (D-Rank: 2d4, 20ft, C-Rank: 4d4, 25ft, B-Rank: 6d4, 30ft A-Rank: 8d4 35ft, S-Rank: 10d4, 40ft)

Wind Release: You strike forward, creating a spear, bullet or blast of wind targeting a creature you can see in range. Make a ranged Taijutsu attack that cannot be made at disadvantage, dealing your [Unarmed Damage] + wind damage equal to the rank of the jutsu cast. Regardless of a hit or miss, you gain a fly speed equal to your movement speed until the end of your next turn. (D-Rank: 3d8, C-Rank: 5d8, B-Rank: 7d8, A-Rank: 9d8, S-Rank: 11d8)

Fire Release: You release a blazing torrent of flame that smolders and explodes forward like a burning missile targeting a creature you can see in range. Make a ranged Taijutsu attack that cannot be made at disadvantage dealing your [Unarmed Damage] + fire damage equal to the rank of the jutsu cast. On a hit, all creatures, except the original target within a 10-foot radius, centered on the target creature must also make a Dexterity or Constitution (your choice) saving throw, taking the rank-based fire damage on a failed save or half as much on a success. (D-Rank: 2d6+2, C-Rank: 4d6+4, B-Rank: 6d6+6, A-Rank: 8d6+8, S-Rank: 10d6+10)

Water Release: You unleash a torrent of crashing waves, overwhelming everyone in your path. All creatures in a 30-foot cone originating from you must make a Strength or Constitution saving throw (your choice). On a failure, you deal your [Unarmed Damage] + cold damage equal to the rank of the jutsu cast blasting the creature to the far edge of the cone, and knocking them prone. Whether they succeed or fail, the overwhelming surge can rip weapons from their grasp, disarming any items they are holding. Structures hit by this jutsu are treated as vulnerable to its damage. (D-Rank: 2d6, C-Rank: 4d6, B-Rank: 6d6, A-Rank: 8d6, S-Rank: 10d6)

Lightning Release: You blitz forward like a flash of light and strike with enough kinetic force to penetrate stone, steel and chakra-based defenses in a single strike. Make a melee Taijutsu attack dealing your [Unarmed Damage] + lightning damage equal to the rank of the jutsu cast. If this attack scores a critical hit, you can recast it as a finisher, targeting a different creature. (D-Rank: 3d8, C-Rank: 5d8, B-Rank: 7d8, A-Rank: 9d8, S-Rank: 11d8)

If you would use any combination of two of these Martial Techniques, as part of a Taijutsu you cast, you must pick which one replaces the Taijutsu’s saving throw, and the other forces a second save to apply its own effects.

You learn two maneuvers of your choice, which are detailed in the Assault Maneuvers Section at the end of this class. You earn more at higher levels as shown in the Maneuvers Known Column of the Scout-Nin Class table. Maneuvers normally enhance your unarmed or Weapon attacks or jutsu you cast in some way. You can use one maneuver per turn as part of an unarmed or weapon attack made with the Attack Action or as part of a Bonus Action attack or as part of a jutsu’s casting. Otherwise, a maneuver will detail its Action economy cost.

As part of your superior skill to lay down oppressive force, you gain a +1 bonus to your critical threat range with attacks made using your Primary casting discipline.

All it takes is a single strike to rattle an enemies skeletal structure, breaking them from the inside out. When you use this technique, they must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, they are Bone Broken. Once you use this Martial Technique you cannot do so again until the end of your next turn.

activities.label: Bone Broken
activities.text: On a failed save (ends at the end of its turn).

system.description:
When you choose this Style, starting at 3rd level, you focus on overwhelming your enemies with more than they could conceivably handle at one time. You learn to accomplish this through a series of Martial Techniques, unique to you and your style of combat. You learn the following Martial Techniques.

Shatter. When a hostile creature casts a Ninjutsu or Genjutsu, you may, as a reaction, spend 1 Martial Die to move up to half your speed, ending your movement as close as possible to the triggering creature. If you end this movement in range of the triggering creature, you can make two unarmed attacks. If at least one of those attacks are successful, the affected creature must make a Chakra control check vs your Taijutsu save DC. On a failed save you Interrupt their jutsu’s casting. On a success, the jutsu is cast normally.

Unstable Drive. When a hostile creature triggers an attack of opportunity from you, in place of the attack made as part of the attack of opportunity, you may spend 1 Martial Die. When you do, you can instead cast a D-Rank Taijutsu targeting them. This becomes C-Rank at 10th and B-Rank at 17th level.

Starting at 1st level, you begin your path to mastery over Chakra and Ninjutsu. This manifests within you as Focus. You carry a number of Focus equal to 1+ proficiency bonus. You can spend this Focus to accomplish feats of control and finesse with Ninjutsu impossible by others of similar skill called Moldings. Normally, you can use one molding as part of a Ninjutsu you cast. Each molding costs 1 Focus unless otherwise specified. You recover spent Focus on a long rest.

You begin knowing two Moldings of your choice found at the end of the class. You learn additional moldings as you grow in level as seen in the Ninjutsu Specialist class chart. You can only use moldings on Ninjutsu you cast without the Combination keyword.

In the eyes of a Scout-Nin following the Path of the Archivist, knowledge is the ultimate weapon. You devour information faster and process that information faster than anyone else. You gain the following benefits;

Encyclopedic Knowledge. When you take the Identify Ninjutsu/Genjutsu/Taijutsu/Bukijutsu action when you make your check, you compare your result to the targets Jutsu save DC (you do not add the +5 to the save DC)

Lore Extraction. You can attempt to Study as a Full-Turn Action, instead of spending 1 minute completing the activity. Additionally, whenever you Research a topic, can choose to hyper fixate for 1 hour gaining a 1d8 bonus instead of spending multiple hours on the topic.

When you cast a Ninjutsu that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, you can give one target of the Jutsu, disadvantage on its first saving throw made against the Jutsu’s effect. You can use this molding in addition to any other moldings you are using.

You adjust your Taijutsu stance to embody the fighting style of a barbarian. Someone who values inflicting as much harm and collateral damage as possible. While you are in a Taijutsu stance you can achieve the following;

Devastating Taijutsu. Once per turn, a Taijutsu you cast gain the Devastating keyword. Taijutsu with the Devastating keyword gain a +1 bonus to their critical threat range.

Unstoppable Force. When a creature you targeted with a Taijutsu spends their reaction to cast a jutsu to summon a construct or structure that would intercept the damage you deal, you can spend your reaction to gain an additional Action, which you can only use to recast the same jutsu, targeting the same creature.

Fueled By Ruin. Beginning at 9th level, Taijutsu you cast with the Devastating keyword that scores a critical hit has some of its chakra cost refunded, as you regain temporary chakra equal to the rank it was cast at. (D-Rank: 2, C-Rank: 3, B-Rank: 4, A-Rank: 5, S-Rank: 6)

castOption.label: Devastating Taijutsu (+1 crit range)
castOption.note: +1 critical threat range on this Taijutsu.

system.description: As an action, you can spend up to 4 Martial Die and move up to your full movement speed in a straight line, passing through any creatures you encounter. When you do, they must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take [Unarmed Damage] + Martial Die equal to the spent amount, are knocked prone and pulled with you to the end of your movement, ending in a space of your choice, adjacent to you that can hold them. This does not affect creatures two or more sizes larger than you.

activities.label: Step of Savagery
activities.text: Up to 4 Martial Dice; creatures in the line are dragged along.

system.description:
When using the Multiattack trait with a Kunai, Shuriken, or Senbon, you can add your ability modifier to the damage rolled. Also, once per turn, while you are gaining the benefits of this generalization you can spend one Superiority Die as part of casting a Jutsu or making an unarmed or weapon attack. When you do, you gain a bonus to the damage dealt equal to 1d8. This bonus increases to 2d8 at 5th, 3d8 at 11th, 4d8 at 15th and 5d8 at 20th level. If used as part of an unarmed attack, weapon attack or jutsu that affects an area or an unarmed or weapon attack, roll half the listed number of dice, rounded up, minimum 1.

If you use a Maneuver granted by your Scouting Technique (Subclass) as part of an attack or jutsu’s casting, you can use this feature as part of that maneuver, reduce the number of bonus damage by 1 dice when you do.

activities.label: Warfare: attack bonus
activities.text: Unarmed or weapon attack (half the dice, rounded up).

system.description: Beginning at 1st level you realize that a shinobi’s strength doesn’t lie in raw power or hyper specialization. It lies in flexibility, adaptation, and awareness in the world around them. This evolving awareness sets you apart from more specialized shinobi, for when others rely on a single discipline, you walk the winding path of versatility. Choose a Shinobi Path below. You gain an additional choice at 11th level.

In the eyes of a Scout-Nin following the Path of Awareness, mastering the unseen is your art, and your perceptive capabilities are your brush to the canvas that is the world. You trained yourself to not only notice what others miss, but to exploit it. You gain the following benefits;

Overly Perceptive. You can use the Search or Identify Genjutsu skill-based actions as a Bonus action.

Sensory Type. As an Action, you can broaden your perceptive abilities allowing you to sense chakra. When you do, make a Wisdom (Perception) check vs the Chakra Control DC of all creatures within 60 feet of you. On a success, you gain the benefit of the Chakra Sensing special sense for the next minute against them for the duration until they either have 0 chakra or they make and succeed their Suppress Chakra skill action.

When you hit a creature with an attack, you can spend a superiority die. When you do, you push the target in a direction away from you. They move a number of feet away equal to 10 x the result of the superiority Die and end this movement falling prone. If your movement would be stopped by a structure no thicker than 5 feet, then structure is destroyed and they continue their movement taking 2d6 bludgeoning damage for each structure they pass through.

roll.note: Push 10 ft × the die, ending Prone; 2d6 bludgeoning per structure it breaks through.

system.description:
When you cast a Ninjutsu with an area of effect, you can increase the size of it.

If the effect is a line, its width is increase by 5 feet or length is increases by 10 feet.

If the effect is a cube or sphere, its radius increases by 5 feet.

If the effect is a cone, its length increases by 10 feet.

If the effect is a cylinder, either the radius or the height increases by 10 feet.

Beginning at 3rd level, select one Taijutsu Stance found in Chapter 13: Customization Options that you do not know as you learn it as well as the Expert feat associated with the Taijutsu stance. The feat gained in this way does not increase your ability score.

When you make an Unarmed or Melee Taijutsu attack, at the conclusion of the attack, you may switch stances instead of spending a bonus action.

Once per turn, when you swap to any stance, you gain a Stance Shift benefit of your choice from the following list. These benefits last until the beginning of your next turn;

Impact Switch. Each time you deal [Unarmed Damage] to a creature you can push them 5 feet into any direction of your choice (Excluding vertically).

Defensive Switch. Each time you deal [Unarmed Damage] to a creature, roll 1 Martial Die, gaining the result as temporary hit points.

Retaliatory Switch. Hostile creatures that cast a Jutsu with the Hand Sign (HS) component while adjacent to you, triggers an attack of opportunity at no reaction cost, once per turn. If you score a hit with an unarmed attack of opportunity the affected creature must make a Strength saving throw vs your Taijutsu save DC, on a failed save, they are knocked prone.

Deflective Switch. The first time each turn you take damage from an attack, roll 1 Martial Die, reducing the damage you take by the result.

Also at 5th Level, you take your skill with chakra network refinement and extend it to your meditations and short downtimes. When you and allied creatures would spend at least 10 uninterrupted minutes resting, you can lead a group meditation where you can roll 1d8, regaining the result as chakra for yourself and all participating allied creatures. A creature can only benefit from this feature once per short rest. This becomes 2d8 at 11th and 3d8 at 17th levels.

activities.label: Group meditation
activities.text: You and participating allies (select their tokens); once per Short Rest each.

system.description:
You adjust your Taijutsu stance to embody the fighting style of a protector or guardian. Someone who values protecting the weak over displaying strength. While you are in a Taijutsu stance you can achieve the following;

Protective Taijutsu. Once per turn, a Taijutsu you cast gain the Protective keyword. Taijutsu with the Protective keyword grants an allied creature within a 10-foot radius, other than its caster, a +1 bonus to their AC for each instance of damage it deals (Max +2)

Guardian Force. When you cast a Taijutsu as a reaction to taking damage or making a saving throw, all allied creatures within a 10-foot radius, other than yourself. They gain the benefits of your Taijutsu for its duration, so long as they remain within 10 feet of you.

Champion. Beginning at 9th level, Taijutsu you cast with the Protective keyword grants all affected allied creatures 10 temporary hit points for each instance of damage dealt (Max 20)

castOption.label: Protective Taijutsu (ally +1 AC)
castOption.note: An ally within 10 ft gains +1 AC per instance of damage (max +2): target the ally.

system.description:
In the eyes of a Scout-Nin following the Path of the Rogue, you become a whisper in the dark, the unseen hand slipping through the cracks of an enemies defenses, making silence, shadow and sleight of hand your main weapons gaining the following benefits;

Veiled Hand. You can use the Steal Action as a Bonus Action and you can use the Pick a Lock action without a Security Kit once per lock as if you have 1 Charge.

Shinobi Step. You can move your full movement when attempting to Sneak.

In the eyes of a Scout-Nin following the Path of the Swift, movement is life. You’ve trained to move like wind through the forests, across rooftops and along sheer canyon walls, not just to escape Danger, but to control the battlefield, gaining the following benefits;

Mastering the Basics. When Wall Running or Water Walking, you do not spend extra movement.

Boosted Athleticism. Increase your movement speed by +10 feet and the height of your High jump and distance of your long jump by 5 feet.

While you are gaining the benefits of this generalization, when you would force a creature to make a saving throw with a Maneuver, item, or feature you use, you can spend 1 Bonus Action. When you do, the affected creature cannot gain bonuses to their saving throw as a result of jutsu they cast. Also, when making a contested check with a hostile creature, you can spend 1 Superiority Die to add the result to your check.

activities.label: Seize: add to a contested check

roll.note: Add the Superiority Die to your contested check.

system.description: When you would take damage from a creature within range of one of your unarmed/weapon attacks or a Jutsu you know, you can spend two superiority die and your reaction. Make an attack or cast a Jutsu targeting the triggering creature. If you score a hit or the affected creature fails their saving throw, you can attack again or cast the same jutsu again, targeting the same creature. If you are making an attack, you do so with a -4 penalty to hit. If they are making a save, they do so with a +4 bonus to their save, repeating the effects of this maneuver on a successful hit or failed save. Each time beyond the first that you repeat this casting or attack, the penalty/bonus increases by -/+ 2 respectively.

roll.note: Attack or cast at the triggering creature; repeat on a hit or failed save (−4 to hit / +4 to its save, growing by 2).

system.description: When you hit a creature with a melee unarmed or Taijutsu attack, you can spend 1 Martial Die to stunt its mobility, forcing it to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, their speed is reduced to 0, and are knocked prone until the beginning of your next turn.

activities.label: Arresting Technique
activities.text: Failure: speed 0 and Prone until the start of your next turn.

system.description: If you make an attack roll for a ninjutsu and you would miss, you can remake the attack roll targeting another creature within range. You must use the result of the second roll. You can use this molding in addition to any other moldings you are using.

You adjust your Taijutsu stance to embody the fighting style of a perfectionist. Someone who doesn’t know the meaning of good enough. While you are in a Taijutsu stance you can achieve the following;

Technical Taijutsu. Once per turn, a Taijutsu you cast gain the Technical keyword. Taijutsu with the Technical keyword that requires concentration allows you to make Martial Arts checks in place of Chakra control checks to maintain concentration.

Unbreakable Focus. Taijutsu you cast cannot have their cost increased by hostile effects.

Perfectionists Musing. Beginning at 9th level, Taijutsu you cast with the Technical keyword that does not affect hostile creatures, cannot be reacted to or dispelled by jutsu of equal rank or lower to them.

castOption.label: Technical Taijutsu
castOption.note: Martial Arts checks in place of Chakra Control to keep its concentration.

system.description: When you cast a Ninjutsu that has a casting time of 1 action, you can change the casting time to 1 bonus action for the casting.
On your turn, by spending 2 Martial Die and all of your movement, you can select a space you can see within your movement range, and teleport into that space.

Finally at 2nd level, you exemplify the ideal of generalized combat. Select one of the following Generalizations between Warfare, Seize and Tactics. When you do, you gain its benefits. You can switch which generalization you have by spending a Bonus Action.

When using the Multiattack trait with a Kunai, Shuriken, or Senbon, you can add your ability modifier to the damage rolled. Also, once per turn, while you are gaining the benefits of this generalization you can spend one Superiority Die as part of casting a Jutsu or making an unarmed or weapon attack. When you do, you gain a bonus to the damage dealt equal to 1d8. This bonus increases to 2d8 at 5th, 3d8 at 11th, 4d8 at 15th and 5d8 at 20th level. If used as part of an unarmed attack, weapon attack or jutsu that affects an area or an unarmed or weapon attack, roll half the listed number of dice, rounded up, minimum 1.

Also at 5th level, once per turn you can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. By spending 2 Superiority Die you can take one additional action on your turn, which can only be used to Cast a Jutsu. This action cannot be used to cast a jutsu of the same casting discipline you previously cast on this turn and you cannot spend your action for the remainder of the turn to cast a jutsu of the same casting discipline as you cast with this feature. If you would use this feature again before you complete a rest, increase the number of Superiority Die you spend to activate this feature by +1 for each time used beyond the first.

roll.note: One extra action this turn to cast a jutsu of a different discipline. Each further use before a rest costs +1 die.

system.description: Also, at 2nd Level your study of Ninshou, chakra and other theoretical and practical applications of ninjutsu gives you a leg up in scholastic use of this knowledge. You gain a rank of Mastery in the Ninshou skill. You gain an additional rank in Mastery for Ninshou at 7th and 13th levels.
When you are hit by a ranged weapon, Ninjutsu or Taijutsu attack, you can spend your Reaction and up to 3 Martial Die. When you do, reduce the damage taken by the result + your level.

roll.note: Reduce the damage taken by this (up to 3 Martial Dice).

system.description:
Also at 1st level, your training with unarmed techniques have granted you a technique that others of your skill level could only ever pray to emulate. This manifests in the form of Martial die, which are d6. Your martial die grows in size, matching the size of your unarmed damage die based on the Martial Strength ability from the Martial Strength class feature.

At the beginning of each of your turns you manifest a pool of martial die, equal to the number shown in the Martial die column of the Taijutsu specialist class table. You can spend your martial die to complete any number of Martial Techniques or Taijutsu specialist class features. Unspent martial die are lost at the beginning of each of your turns.

You begin with two known martial techniques, learning more as noted in the Martial techniques column of the Taijutsu Specialist class table. Martial Techniques are detailed at the end of this class description and uses your Taijutsu save DC if they require a save of any type.

Also, at 3rd level, you learn to harness your elemental chakra to enhance your combat potential. You learn to accomplish this through a series of Martial Techniques, unique to you and your style of combat. You learn the following Martial Techniques.

Elemental Rush. Whenever you hit a creature with a melee Taijutsu attack you can spend 1 Martial Die. When you do, you can spend your bonus action to cast 1 D-Rank Ninjutsu with the same nature release whose casting time is 1 Action, using your Taijutsu ability modifier in place of your Ninjutsu ability modifier. The Ninjutsu ranks you can cast as part of this feature increases to C-Rank at 10th level and B-Rank at 17th level.

Elemental Crush. When you cast a Taijutsu with the Finisher keyword and are able to utilize its Finisher effects, you can spend 1 Martial Die to instead use your Elemental Finisher in its place. You still spend the chakra cost as if casting the Jutsu, but you apply your Elemental Finishers effects in its place. This is still treated as a Finisher. You can use this Martial Technique once per turn.

Also, at 1st level, your speed is increased by +10 and you can Dash as a Bonus action. This bonus to speed increases to +15 and your jump distance is doubled when you take the Dash action at 5th level. The bonus to speed increases to +20 at 11th level, +25 at 15th level, and +30 at 20th level.

Also, at 2nd level your style thrives on switching approaches. You blend casting disciplines with such skill that your transitions become strengths, not weaknesses. First, select your Primary casting discipline keyword (Ninjutsu, Genjutsu, Taijutsu and Bukijutsu). The chosen casting discipline becomes the lynchpin of your form of fighting. When you cast your Primary jutsu, you set up a strong follow up for the next jutsu. You cannot select a keyword as your Primary if your keywords casting ability modifier is lower than another casting ability modifier. (Ex. You cannot select Ninjutsu as your primary, if your Taijutsu ability modifier is higher than your Ninjutsu ability score.) When you cast your Primary casting discipline, you can choose to either Follow Up, or Set-Up.

Follow Up. One affected creature grants you a +1 bonus to hit or to your Jutsu save DC against them if the next jutsu cast affecting them is not your Primary casting discipline. This becomes a +2 a 11th and +3 at 19th level. This bonus to hit and save DC lasts until the end of your next turn.

Set-Up. All affected creatures suffers a -1 penalty to their AC or Saving throw (your choice) against the next jutsu cast from one of your allies (excluding you) before the beginning of your next turn. This becomes a -2 at 11th and -3 at 19th level.

activities.label: Follow Up
activities.text: +1 (11th +2, 19th +3) to hit or to your save DC against it with your next non-Primary jutsu.

system.description:
Scout-Nin Keyword: Specialized

When you deal damage to your Combat Rival as a result of an attack, you can spend one superiority die recording the result. Select a number of creatures within 10 feet of the target equal to the result of the superiority die. You and compare the result of your attack to their AC. If your attack would hit, they take half the damage you dealt to your Combat Rival.

roll.note: That many creatures within 10 ft: if your attack hits their AC, they take half the damage.

system.description:
In the eyes of a Scout-Nin following the Path of the Commandant, a plan wins fights before the first-hand sign is ever made. You’ve studied battlefield tactics, choke points and ambush tactics. Your presence on a team isn’t just help, it’s a force multiplier. You gain the following benefits;

Field Strategist. You can take the Help Action as a Bonus action even with skills you do not have proficiency in.

Tactical Callouts. Once per turn, when an allied creature is the target of an attack or jutsu’s effect, you can use your reaction to move up to half your movement closer to them and if you end your movement within 15 feet of them, you command them to take cover, granting them a +2 bonus to their AC or saving throw against the triggering attack or saving throw.

When you choose this Style starting at 3rd level, your body moves with unstoppable rhythm, every strike flowing into the next like crashing waves, with each blow fueling the next, building an unrelenting tempo that drives you toward a single, devastating finish.

When you cast a Taijutsu with the Combo keyword, you enter a state of combat rhythm you call your DYNAMIC FORM!. Which lasts until you cast a Taijutsu with the Finisher keyword or initiative ends, whichever happens first. While in your DYNAMIC FORM! state, each time you cast a Taijutsu with the Combo keyword, you gain 1 Tempo (Max 3). You lose 1 Tempo at the end of each of your turns, where you didn’t cast a Taijutsu with the Combo keyword. While you have Tempo you gain passive bonuses based on the number of Tempo you have. When you cast a Taijutsu with the Finisher keyword, you immediately spend all accumulated Tempo, gaining cumulative bonuses based on the amount of Tempo spent.

Passive Tempo Benefits. While you have tempo, you gain the following benefits.

1 Tempo. While you have 1 tempo, you gain a rank of Mastery with Athletics and Acrobatics based skill actions and you can ignore difficult terrain.

2 Tempo. While you have 2 tempo, you can move through enemy spaces, and attacks of opportunities against you are made at disadvantage.

3 Tempo. While you have 3 tempo, you gain a +1 bonus to Taijutsu attacks critical threat range and your Taijutsu save DC.

Finisher Tempo Benefits. When you cast a Taijutsu finisher, you spend all tempo you have, gaining cumulative benefits for each tempo spent.

1 Tempo. When you spend 1 tempo, you can use one Martial Technique at no Martial Die cost.

2 Tempo. When you spend 2 tempo, if the jutsu requires an attack, you can now compare the attack results to the AC of all creatures in a 5-foot radius around the original target, affecting them with the jutsu as well on a successful hit. This increases to 10-feet at 10th level and 15 feet at 17th level.

3 Tempo. When you spend 3 tempo, if you score a critical hit or the affected creature fails their saving throw by 5 or more, you regain the action spent casting the jutsu.

roll.note: Each Combo Taijutsu in DYNAMIC FORM!; lose 1 at the end of a turn without one.

system.description:
Scout-Nin Keyword: Specialized

When you fail a saving throw that would both deal damage and inflict a condition, you can spend 1 Superiority Die, adding the result to your save. If this would cause you to instead succeed, you release a surge of chakra with enough pressure to overtake anyone near you. On a success, all hostile creatures within 20 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw vs your Jutsu save DC. On a failure, they become Dazed until the beginning of your next turn.

roll.note: Add the die to your failed save; if you now succeed, hostiles within 20 ft make a Wisdom save or are Dazed.

system.description: Starting at 2nd level, you begin to Specialize in a Tradition that enhances the style of ninjutsu that you focus on. The Tradition that you choose grants you features at 2nd, 6th, 10th, 14th & 18th Levels.
Beginning at 1st Level you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the Chakra Stances located in Chapter 13: Customization Options.
When a creature would trigger an attack of opportunity, by spending 1 Martial Die, you can make two unarmed attacks in place of one.

You adjust your Taijutsu stance to embody the fighting style of a prodigy. Someone whose skills and technique comes along once in a generation to usher in a new form of fighting. While you are in a Taijutsu stance you can achieve the following;

Elite Taijutsu. Once per turn, a Taijutsu you cast gain the Elite keyword. Taijutsu with the Elite keyword gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls.

The New Era. Increase the Taijutsu save DC of Taijutsu you cast that forces a creature to make a saving throw, by +1.

Next Generation. Beginning at 9th level, Taijutsu you cast with the Elite keyword that forces a creature to make a Chakra control check to maintain concentration, can instead force the target to make an Athletics check.

Starting at 2nd Level, your attacks become imbued with your chakra, enhancing each strike into becoming more and more lethal as more chakra is packed behind each blow.

The first time you deal damage on a turn as a result of the Attack action or a Taijutsu you cast, you can use either the Sustained Pressure or Valve Break abilities.

Sustained Pressure. By spending 1 Martial Die, the triggering unarmed attack and every subsequent unarmed attack for the remainder of the turn adds your Martial Die to the damage dealt.

Valve Break. When you cast a Taijutsu that deals damage, you can spend 1 Martial Die. When you do, you add a number of Martial Die to its damage equal to the rank of the jutsu cast. (D-Rank: 1, C-Rank: 2, B-Rank: 3, A-Rank: 4, S-Rank: 5)

activities.label: Sustained Pressure
activities.text: This and every later unarmed attack this turn adds a Martial Die.

castOption.label: Valve Break (1 Martial Die: +rank Martial Dice)
castOption.note: The first time you deal damage this turn.

system.description:
Scout-Nin Keyword: Specialized

When you cast a jutsu that forces your Combat Rival to make a saving throw of any kind to resist gaining a condition, you can spend a superiority die. When you do, if the affected creature(s) fail their saving throw, they gain +1 ranks of that condition.

As an Action, by spending 4 Martial Die you move at such speeds you vanish from sight. Select up to 4 creatures within range of your movement speed, and make a single unarmed attack comparing your results against each of their AC’s, and then teleporting into a space adjacent to one of them. On a hit, you deal your [Unarmed Damage] + 4 Martial Die and must make a Constitution saving throw, being Staggered on a failed save.

activities.label: Hurricane Strikes
activities.text: One roll against up to 4 creatures, then teleport next to one.

system.description: By spending 1 Martial Die, creatures cannot react to your movement and you move without making sounds or leaving tracks.

Beginning at 1st level, your practice of martial arts gives you master of your body in both an offensive and defensive way. While you are wearing no armor, your AC equals 10 + Proficiency + Dexterity Modifier.

Also, choose one Taijutsu stance and its associated Expertise located in Chapter 13: Customization Options. You also gain the following benefits while you are in a Taijutsu Stance or wielding a weapon you are proficient in:

Martial Strength. Your unarmed damage die is a d6. This increases to a d8 at 7th, d10 at 13th level and d12 at 19th levels.

Agile Combat. You can use Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls and Save DC calculation of your unarmed strikes, Taijutsu and the Martial Arts skill. You can also make one unarmed attack as a Bonus action.

Unwasted Movements. When you use Taijutsu, you waste little energy. Taijutsu you cast have a predetermined base chakra cost based on its rank unless its cost is already Special in which case you use the prewritten Special cost. The following values are treated as Special and cannot be combined with other sources of cost reduction. (D-Rank: 3, C-Rank: 5, B-Rank: 9, A-Rank: 14, S-Rank: 20)

While you are gaining the benefits of this generalization, when you use a skill-based action that require an Action, it can be performed as a Bonus action. Once per turn, If a skill-based action costs a reaction, you can use it at no action cost.

Also, you can spend one superiority die as part of a Skill-based action, adding a +2 bonus to the check. This bonus increases to+3 at 11th, +4 at 20th level.

roll.note: Add this to the skill-based action's check.

system.description: As a Bonus action, on your turn, you draw on your bodies self-restoration potential, magnifying it by spending 2 Martial Die. You regain hit points equal to the result + your Taijutsu ability modifier. Once you use this technique, you cannot do so again until you complete a rest.

activities.label: Regenerative Surge
activities.text: Once per rest.

system.description: When you would see a creature within 90 feet of you cast a Ninjutsu that would deal damage of any type, you may as a reaction cast a Ninjutsu you know with a casting time of 1 action. When you do, if the jutsu you cast doesn’t have the clash keyword it gains the clash keyword. You automatically initiate a clash with the triggering creatures jutsu even if their jutsu doesn’t have the clash keyword.

Scout-Nin Keyword: Specialized

When you deal damage to your Combat Rival, you can spend one superiority die. All creatures of your choice within 20 feet of you or the original target (pick one) must make a Wisdom saving throw vs the Attack or Jutsu’s save DC (If Weapon/Unarmed, Taijutsu save DC) as your attack releases a menacing aura. On a failed save, affected creature gains ranks of Demoralized equal to half the result of your Superiority die.

activities.label: Menacing Assault
activities.text: Creatures of your choice within 20 ft; failure: Demoralized ranks = half the Superiority Die.

system.description:
Also at 1st level, you have learned to compress your chakra into a more efficient state when casting Ninjutsu, increasing your efficiency beyond the pale. Once per turn, when you cast a Ninjutsu as an Action, you may compress your chakra into a more efficient state, conserving your stamina. When you do, reduce the cost of the jutsu cast by an amount equal to its rank (D-Rank: 1, C-Rank: 2, B-Rank: 3, A-Rank: 4, S-Rank: 5).

Beginning at 11th level, your ability to compress your chakra has amplified and become far more prescient. By spending 1 Focus you can cast a Ninjutsu without the Combination keyword, with the casting time of 1 Action, at D-Rank, at 0 Chakra cost. This becomes C-Rank or lower at 17th level.

In the eyes of a Scout-Nin following the Path of the Mender, you understand that even the sharpest blade dulls in isolation. You walk a path of stabilization, bringing focus, healing and calm during and after a heated battle gaining the following benefits;
