Field Medic. You can use the Administer Aid skill action as a bonus action.

Battle Medicine. You can use the Treat Wounds skill action as an Action.

At no action cost, on your turn, you can spend 1 superiority die to temporarily unleash your limits, with the drawback of sacrificing your defenses. Until the beginning of your next turn, you gain the following benefits. If you would use this maneuver again before completing a rest, increase the number of Superiority Die you spend to activate this feature by +1 for each time used beyond the first.

You cannot be reduced below 1 HP as a result of damage from an attack or Jutsu. (Conditional damage can still reduce you to 0 HP)

You add your superiority die to the first attack roll you make each turn.

The first attack targeting you each turn is made at advantage.

activities.label: Limit Breaker
activities.text: Until your next turn: can't drop below 1 HP from attacks or jutsu; add the die to your first attack roll each turn; the first attack against you each turn has advantage. More uses before a rest cost +1 die each.

system.description: You cast a jutsu that pierces through a creature’s defenses. When you cast a Ninjutsu that deals damage it ignores resistance, and half of a creatures DR (Damage Reduction). Creatures that are normally Immune to the damage your jutsu deals, you instead treat their immunity as resistance.

When you deal unarmed damage to a creature as a result of an attack, you can spend 1 Martial Die to force them to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, they are pushed back a number of feet equal to 5 times the result. Beginning at 7th level, you can spend 2 dice increasing the distance pushed and at 13th level, you can spend 3 dice. If a pushed creatures movement would be stopped by a solid structure or objected, they and the object/structure take 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 5 feet of movement the affected creature did not move.

roll.note: Feet pushed on a failure (1d6 per bludgeoning per 5 ft short if stopped).

system.description: Also at 2nd level, while they were partying, you hardened your fists. While they were making hand signs, you learned to punch holes in steel. While they played mind games with Genjutsu, you kicked the tree 1000 times. Now that they are in battle and they can’t take a punch, they have the audacity to come to you. So be it. Select one of the following Paths of Perfection. These paths represent your hard work. Your tenacity and your technique. Some paths interact with Taijutsu stances in unique ways.

You don’t need Ninjutsu to arrest your falling speed. That’s what squats are for. When you would take falling damage, you can spend up to 3 Martial Die. When you do, reduce the number of damage die rolled by twice the result.

roll.note: Fewer falling damage dice by this many (up to 3 Martial Dice).

system.description: When you would cast a Taijutsu, you can spend 1 martial die. When you do, the jutsu cast gains the Technical keyword. Jutsu with the Technical keyword reduces the cost to maintain concentration on it by an amount equal to half the result of the die.

castOption.label: Technical Technique (1 Martial Die)
castOption.note: Concentration upkeep reduced by half the roll.

system.description:
Scout-Nin Keyword: Specialized

When you score critical hit against your Combat Rival, you can spend 1 superiority die. Reduce the targets AC and DR, by an amount equal to half the result of the superiority die. Your Combat Rival for the duration of the penalty, cannot gain jutsu based bonuses to its AC or DR. This penalty lasts until the beginning of your next turn.

activities.label: Rending Critical
activities.text: Your Combat Rival on a critical hit; it can't gain jutsu bonuses to AC or DR meanwhile.

system.description: As a reaction, on your turn, you can cast a ninjutsu with a casting time of 1 action.

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Additionally at 11th level, when you take the attack action, you may as a bonus action make 2 unarmed attacks.

Moment of Stillness – Balance Broken

Balance Broken is treated as a Physical Condition. Creatures with it are have had their balance thrown off, finding it difficult to recover. The suffer the following effects.

Disadvantage on Strength Saving throws.

Cannot gain bonuses to AC or DR as a result of Jutsu.

If an affected creature would willingly move more than 5 feet or cast a Jutsu with the Mobility (M) component, they must spend their Reaction to maintain balance, otherwise, they fall prone, unable to stand until the beginning of their next turn.

This condition ends at the end of an affected creatures turn.

Also at 3rd level, your technique is weaponized to drift between a myriad of fighting styles to defeat your enemies.

You learn to accomplish this through a series of Martial Techniques, unique to you and your style of combat. You learn the following Martial Techniques.

Style Shift. When a creature makes an attack targeting you, you may as a reaction spend 1 Martial die. When you do, you may switch your Taijutsu stance and make an unarmed attack against the triggering creature. On a hit, you force the target creature to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, they become Dazed.

Dodge Cancel. When you hit a creature with a melee Taijutsu or Unarmed attack, you can spend 1 Martial die. When you do, you can switch your Taijutsu stance and take a defensive stance. The next attack the damaged creature makes against you until the beginning of your next turn is made at disadvantage.

Beginning at 2nd level, your chakra burns hotter, faster and brighter than others. But this flame doesn’t simply go out. Instead, it keeps burning until reaching its full potential. Once per turn, when you would cast a Jutsu with the Fire Release keyword, you gain 1 Pyroclasm, represented as a burning ember of flame on your body in a fashion of your choice, with a max of 3 Pyroclasm that can be maintained. You can ignite Pyroclasm on the following abilities (Igniting Pyroclasm spends them).

Detonate. As an Action, you ignite any number of Pyroclasm of your choice, releasing a shockwave of burning fire chakra. All creatures within 10 feet of you must make a Dexterity saving throw vs your Ninjutsu save DC. On a failed save, affected creatures take 2d6 fire damage and gain 1 rank of Burned for each Pyroclasm spent.

Hellrend. As part of the same action used to cast a Ninjutsu with the fire release keyword, that deal fire damage you can ignite any number of Pyroclasm, reducing affected creature's DR (Damage Reduction) by 2 for each Pyroclasm spent until the end of your next turn.

Devastation. As part of the same action used to cast a Ninjutsu with the Fire Release keyword, that deals fire damage you can ignite 1 Pyroclasm. When you do, roll 1d6, maximizing a number of the triggering damage dice equal to half the result, rounded down, to a minimum of 1.

activities.label: Detonate
activities.text: 10 ft around you. Failed save: the damage and 1 rank of Burned per Pyroclasm spent.

castOptions.label: Devastation (1 Pyroclasm)
castOptions.note: Maximize that many damage dice, halved (round down), minimum 1.

system.description: When you cast a Ninjutsu, you can cast it without any hand signs. You can use this molding in addition to any other moldings you are using.

When you would cast a Taijutsu that requires an attack, you can spend 1 Martial Die. When you do, you force creatures of your choice within 5 feet of the original target to make a Dexterity saving throw, taking half of the damage dealt on a failed save, once per casting.

castOption.label: Shockwave Strike (1 Martial Die)
castOption.note: Creatures within 5 ft of the target: Dexterity save or half the damage.

system.description: Starting at 3rd level, choose a technique that you strive to emulate in combat and style. The Scouting Technique you choose grants you features at 3rd, 6th, 10th, 14th and 17th levels.

When you choose this tradition at 2nd Level, you gain the ability to learn ninjutsu with the Fire Release Keyword. If you already have access to this nature release, you learn 2 Fire Release Ninjutsu that you qualify for, one of which can be C-Rank or lower. You can also learn and create Ninjutsu with the Fire Release Keyword in half the required time.

When you choose this Style starting at 3rd level, unlike other Taijutsu specialist, you focus on magnifying your already spectacular skills and talents. Unlike others, your genius is natural and it becomes more pronounced as you grow in your role.

When you roll initiative, your body naturally drifts into a state of instinctual self-weaponization known as becoming Flawless. You remain in this state for the duration of combat, exiting it when combat ends. While in your Flawless state you gain access to Perfection. Once per turn, when you spend at least 1 Martial Die, you gain a Perfection, of which, you can maintain up to 4. You can spend Perfection on the following abilities. You can only use each

Flawless Disturbance. Once per turn, by spending 2 Perfection on a hostile creatures turn, you gain an additional reaction, which can only be used to cast a Taijutsu. This additional reaction lasts until the end of the current turn. You can gain 1 reaction in this way until the beginning of your next turn.

Flawless Focus. Once per turn, you can spend 1 Perfection in place of any 1 Martial Die expenditure. When you do, you still roll your Martial Die as required, but it is not spent from your pool.

Flawless Stances. Once per turn, by spending 1 Perfection, you can switch your current Taijutsu Stance, in place of spending your Bonus action. When you do, the next attack that targets you before the beginning of your next turn is made at disadvantage.

Flawless Technique. When you would roll a Martial Die you can spend 1 Perfection. Roll your Martial Die at advantage, taking the higher result, and applying it to the triggering effect.

Flawless Tempo. Once per turn, when you cast a Taijutsu with the Combo keyword, you can spend 2 Perfection. When you do, the next Taijutsu you cast gains the Combo Extender keyword from the Passionate Taijutsu specialist subclass and you can cast a Taijutsu with the Finisher keyword as a Reaction until the end of your current turn.

roll.note: When you spend at least 1 Martial Die (Flawless state).
Flawless Disturbance and the other Perfection abilities.

system.description: When you are forced to make a concentration check to maintain a ninjutsu you have cast, you can automatically pass the concentration check. You can use this molding in addition to any other moldings you are using.

You adjust your Taijutsu stance to embody the fighting style of a tyrant. Someone who takes away an opponent’s options for hope. While you are in a Taijutsu stance you can achieve the following;

Brutal Taijutsu. Once per turn, a Taijutsu you cast gain the Brutal keyword. Taijutsu with the Brutal keyword increases the damage they deal by +2. This increases to +4 at 11th level.

Stolen Hope. When a creature attempts to cast a jutsu that has a Hand signs (HS) component while adjacent to you, allows you to take the Attack Action as a reaction targeting them.

Victimizer. Beginning at 9th level, Taijutsu you cast with the Brutal keyword that inflicts a Physical condition cannot have their saving throw made at advantage.

When you cast a Ninjutsu that targets only one creature and doesn’t have a range of self, you can target a second creature in range with the same Jutsu. To be eligible for Doubled Ninjutsu, a Ninjutsu must be incapable of targeting more than one creature at the jutsu’s current rank.
When you would cast a Taijutsu, you can spend up to 2 Martial Die. When you do, the jutsu cast gains a +1 bonus to hit for each die spent.

castOption.label: Precise Technique (+1 to hit per die)

system.description:
Beginning at 3rd level you have learned a technique allowing you to enter a heightened state of chakra potency, called a chakra surge, but unlike other battle states, this one just like your Ninjutsu is flexible in its purpose and use. You have two different battle states you can enter; Crash and Flow. You can enter one of these states as a bonus action and once per turn, can spend a bonus action to swap states. You cannot benefit from both states at once and if you would attempt to enter either Crash or Flow while benefiting from the other, you exit the state you are currently in first. When you activate this feature to enter either state, you can remain in either state for a combined duration of up to 1 minute and you cannot re-enter either state until you have spent 10 minutes of uninterrupted time resting or meditating.

Crash

Will Amp

Crash symbolizes you releasing the limits on your chakra coils, empowering the jutsu you cast.

Once per casting, you gain a +1d10 bonus to damage you deal with Ninjutsu you cast. This increases to +2d10 at 7th, 3d10 at 11th, 4d10 at 15th and 5d10 at 19th level. Reduce the dice rolled by half (rounded up) if the jutsu affects an area.

You can use two or more Moldings at once as part of the same casting.

You can use the Draw Reserves skill Action, as an Action.

You cannot benefit from any source of cost reduction. Casting a Jutsu at 0 Cost does not count as cost reduction.

Flow (Will Amp)

Flow symbolizes you controlling and refining your chakra, making slight adjustments to it as the battle progresses.

You gain a +1 bonus to your Ninjutsu Save DC. This bonus increases to +2 at 11th level and +3 at 19th level.

When you being your turn in this state, you regain 1 Focus.

You make Concentration checks to maintain Ninjutsu at advantage.

You cannot benefit from Jutsu or features that boosts the damage you deal with Ninjutsu.

Also at 1st Level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the Fighting Stances located in Chapter 13: Customization Options, between Taijutsu Stance, Weapon Stance and Chakra Mode(s). You select an additional Fighting stance of a type you have not selected from at 7th and 11th levels. You can’t take a Stance more than once.

Also, when fighting with basic Shinobi implements (Kunai, Shuriken, Senbon’s), when you take the attack action you can attack twice, instead of once, with these weapons. If you do, you cannot make an attack with them as a Bonus Action the same turn.

Finally, you can use the following tools in place of an attack made with your Attack Action; Chili Pepper Bombs, Paper Bombs, Flash Tags or Smoke Bombs.

When you hit a creature with an unarmed attack, you can spend 5 Martial Die to infuse its body with vibrations that can shatter their bones. At the end of each of their turns, the affected creature must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take 5 Martial Dice worth of bludgeoning damage, which cannot be reduced or ignored by any means. On a successful save, they end this effect. A creature can only be under the effect of this technique once per rest.

activities.label: Quivering Strike
activities.text: At the end of each of its turns; can't be reduced; a success ends it.

system.description:
Also at 3rd level, a master of relentless engagement, you have refined your fighting style into an unbroken chain of calculated strikes and precision movements. In the hands of a true martial artist, even the simplest movement becomes part of an unstoppable assault.

Once per turn, when you make an Unarmed attack, you can use either a Shove, Trip or Grapple skill action as part of that attack, using your attack bonus as the check result, also dealing your [Unarmed Damage] on a hit.

You also learn to use a series of Martial Techniques, unique to you and your style of combat. You learn the following Martial Techniques.

Chakra Enhanced Blows. You channel Chakra into your hands enhancing your blows even further. When you make an unarmed attack or cast a Taijutsu, you can spend 1 Martial Die, selecting either Sustained Pressure or Valve Break following their effect requirements and applying its effect at no additional Martial Die cost. Additionally, Creatures who fail their saving throw against the Taijutsu cast or are hit two or more times by your unarmed attacks, gain a rank of Bruised.

Tempo Boost. While you have Tempo, when you cast a Taijutsu with the Finisher keyword, you can spend 1 Martial Die. When you do, the jutsu can still be casts ignoring its listed casting time, but it loses the Finisher keyword, instead gaining the Combo Extender keyword. You do not benefit from the jutsu’s finisher effect.

At 3rd level you learn a Combat style that fits in with how you view combat and encompasses your overall approach towards Taijutsu. Your Style grants you feature at 3rd Level and again at 6th, 10th, 14th and 17th Level.

You adjust your Taijutsu stance to embody the fighting style of a predator who is hunting for its prey. Someone who stalks and strikes at their victim until they can no longer run. While you are in a Taijutsu stance you can achieve the following;

Furious Taijutsu. Once per turn, a Taijutsu you cast gain the Furious keyword. Taijutsu with the Furious keyword that deal damage to a target reduces its DR by -2 for each instance of damage dealt. This reduction lasts until end of your next turn.

Can’t Run. Each time you deal unarmed damage to a creature, you reduce their speed by 5 feet until the end of your next turn.

Never Escaping. Beginning at 9th level, Taijutsu you cast with the Furious keyword that targets or affects a creature whose movement speed is 0, can have their first attack per turn made at advantage, or the affected creature makes their first saving throw per turn against them at disadvantage.

activities.label: Can't Run
activities.text: Each time you deal unarmed damage to it.

system.description:
Also at 3rd level, your talent and focus is weaponized to completely drive home the point that it doesn’t matter how much your enemies train to overcome you, they are out of their league and they need to come to grips with this new reality they find themselves in.

You learn to accomplish this through a series of Martial Techniques, unique to you and your style of combat. You learn the following Martial Techniques.

Redirected Aggression. When a hostile creature makes a melee or ranged attack, you may as a reaction, spend one Martial die reducing their attack by the result. If their attack would miss, you can redirect it back towards them by making a melee or ranged unarmed attack, using the missed attacks original range as your attacks range. On a hit, the creature suffers the effects of their original attack plus 1 Martial Die in additional damage.

Shatterpoint. When you deal [Unarmed Damage], you can spend 1 Martial die. When you do, the affected creature must make a Strength Saving throw. On a failed save, they become Shattered.

Shatterpoint – Shattered

Your defenses have been sundered and exposed. Shattered is a physical condition.

Attacks targeting a Shattered creatures gain a +1 bonus to their critical threat range.

A Shattered creature that suffers a critical hit takes bonus damage equal to 2 Martial Die. This increases to 3 Martial Die at 10th and 4 Martial Die at 17th level.

A Shattered creature Increases damage taken by +2. This increases to +4 if the inflictor is 10th level and +6 at 17th level.

The first time you succeed a Strength, Dexterity or Constitution saving throw while you are Shattered, you must remake your saving throw, subtracting the result of 1 Martial Die, taking the lower result. This condition ends immediately.

A Shattered creature can spend their action making a DC 20 Strength check to end this condition on a success.

When you cast a Ninjutsu that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can protect some creatures from the Jutsu’s full force. Select up to 4 creatures. A chosen creature suffers no effect from your casted Ninjutsu.
Whenever you would cast a Ninjutsu that deals damage, after damage is rolled, you can select up to 3 damage die, you treat each selected die as the maximum possible result.

Unlike other casters, you fight with your fist, and your mind. You wrap your arms and legs in your combat scroll providing you with a very different fighting style. You gain the following benefits:

You can now make melee attacks with your Combat Scroll as you strike with chakra covered fists and feet.

While in this stance, your [Unarmed Damage] type becomes the scrolls damage type.

In place of increasing the scrolls damage pool, you instead make a number of attacks equal to the number of dice you would roll, dealing 1d12 damage for each successful hit.

Ninjutsu or Genjutsu you cast that requires an attack, with a range greater than 5 feet, can be cast with a range of 5 feet and are treated as a melee attack. If they are, on a hit, they add 1d12 to their damage dealt once per turn, as your deliver the jutsu’s effect with a scroll covered strike.

Evocation Technique – Twin Scroll Fist. If you have a Strength modifier of +1 or higher, you can wield 2 Giant Combat Scrolls, but they must share the same damage type. While you do, you can select one Taijutsu stance you know. You can benefit from that stances base effects. You cannot benefit from their level 5 or 10 effects. You use 1d12, in place of their unarmed damage die for any effects that require it.

You master the unpredictable arcs and entangling chains of flail weapons, making every swing a threat from unexpected angles. Weapons that qualify for this stance are known as Reaper Weapons. You gain the following benefits;

When a creature within your weapons range misses you with an attack, you can spend your reaction to make an Attack of opportunity against them.

Once per turn, when you make a weapon attack or a melee Taijutsu attack using a Reaper Weapon, you can replace one attack with a Reaping Swing.

Reaping Swing. Make a weapon attack against a creature. On a hit, deal your [Weapon Damage] and force them to make a Dexterity saving throw vs your Taijutsu save DC. On a failure, their DR is reduced by 2 until the start of your next turn.

Beginning at 5th level, when you make an attack of opportunity as a result of a creature missing you with an attack, while using this stance, you can replace that attack with a Reaping Swing.

Beginning at 10th level, the DR penalty from Reaping Swing increases to 4. Additionally, as part of using Reaping Swing, you can select up to 3 creatures weapons range, and have the attack affect each of these spaces. If a creature is in the chosen space, compare the attack result to their AC, treating it as a successful hit on a success

activities.label: Reaping Swing: DR penalty
activities.text: On a failed Dexterity save.

system.description:
You have learned to enter an irregular and erratic fighting style. Attacking with no warning and defending with unconventional motions.

Your Unarmed damage die becomes a d6.

Taijutsu you cast as a Reaction, cannot trigger reactions from hostile creatures.

As a reaction to taking damage from a melee or ranged attack, you can reduce the damage taken by rolling your [Unarmed Damage] twice, taking the higher value and subtracting the result.

Beginning at 5th level, when you use this stances reaction, you also imposes disadvantage on all subsequent attack rolls the triggering creature makes targeting you until the end of the current turn. For each attack they make against you after the first, they also take your [Unarmed Damage] as you retaliate with each strike.

Beginning at 10th level, if you spent your reaction to use this stances reaction ability, at the beginning of the following turn, you gain the special action, Drunken Turn.

Drunken Turn. This special action can only be spent as a reaction to use the Drunken Fist Stances reaction ability. You can gain this special action once, before the end of your next turn.

roll.note: Subtract this from the damage you take (Unarmed Damage rolled twice, higher).

system.description:
You master the blade. All bladed weapons become extensions of your body as their attacks into your very movement. Weapons that qualify for this stance are known as Ronin Weapons. You gain the following benefits:

When you make an opportunity attack with a Ronin Weapon, you have advantage on the attack roll.

When you score a critical hit with a weapon attack using a Ronin Weapon, the target gains 1 rank of Bleeding.

Hostile creatures that cast a Jutsu with the Mobility (M) component trigger an opportunity attack from you.

Beginning at 5th level, when you make a weapon attack or a melee Taijutsu attack using a Ronin Weapon, you can replace one attack with a Bleeding Edge Strike.

Bleeding Edge. Make a weapon attack against a creature. On a hit, deal your [Weapon Damage]. For each rank of Bleeding the target has, the attack deals +2 additional damage.

Beginning at 10th level, creatures that stand up from Prone within your reach also trigger an opportunity attack from you. Also, when you score a critical hit with a Ronin Weapon, the target gains an additional +1 rank of Bleeding.

activities.label: Bleeding Edge
activities.text: +2 damage for each rank of Bleeding the target has.

system.description:
You are skilled at putting the weight of a weapon to your advantage. All large or unwieldy weapons, are just additional tools to add to your toolbelt. Weapons that qualify for this stance are known as Berserker Weapons. You gain the following benefits;

When you roll a 1 or 2 on with your [Weapon Damage] die, you can reroll the die, keeping the second result.

When you make a successful weapon attack against a hostile creature, you deal half of the damage dealt to other hostile creatures whom you are adjacent to as you cleave through in an arc.

When you score a critical hit with a Berserker Weapon, double your ability modifier as well.

Beginning at 5th level when you make a weapon attack or a melee Taijutsu attack using a Berserker Weapon, you can replace one attack with a Savage Attack.

Savage Attack. Make a weapon attack against a creature. On a hit, increase your [Weapon Damage] by +1 die. If you make this attack against a creature that has dealt damage to you since your last turn, make it at advantage.

Beginning at 10th level, when you make a Savage Attack, the affected creature must make a Strength saving throw vs your Taijutsu save DC. On a failure, they are knocked Prone and if they attempt to stand before the end of their next turn, they spend all their movement doing so.

activities.label: Savage Attack
activities.text: Advantage against a creature that damaged you since your last turn.

system.description:
When casting a Ninjutsu that summons or creates a construct or structure, your control allows you far more flexibility. You gain the following benefits:

When you cast a Ninjutsu you know that creates a construct weapon, you can downcast it, reducing its cost by 3 and reducing the step of its damage die by 1 step for each rank it is downcast, down to a minimum of D-Rank. If cast in this way, it gains the Stable or Efficient keyword, pick one.

Ninjutsu you cast that summons a wall or structure, increases the height and length of the wall or structure by 10 feet.

Evocation Technique – Polymerization. While wielding a Combat Scroll, when you summon a construct creature, you can select a separate jutsu you know that summons a different construct creature. Select one of their features or attacks. The creature you summoned gains the chosen feature or attack.
system.requirement: Have a Ninjutsu that creates or summons constructs or structures on your known list.

system.description:
You have learned to enter the aggressive and fast paced Wolf Fang fighting stance. You fight with both hands as claws. Each strike aiming for a creature sensitive organs attempting to cause bludgeoning damage on each strike.

Your [Unarmed Damage] die becomes a d6.

As an action, you perform the Wolf Fang Fist.

Wolf Fang Fist. Make two unarmed attacks, increasing your [Unarmed Damage] die by +1.

Beginning at 5th level, As part of using Wolf Fang Fist, before making any attacks, you let out a battle cry. All allied creatures within 30 feet of you that can hear you gain a +1 bonus to their next attack roll or saving throw, whichever comes first, which lasts until the start of your next turn.

Beginning at 10th level, Wolf Fang Fist now makes three unarmed attacks instead of two and the battle cry bonus increases to +2. If you reduce a creature to 0 hit points as a result of these attacks, the bonus lasts until the end of each allies creatures turns.

activities.label: Wolf Fang Fist
activities.text: 5th: battle cry, allies within 30 ft get +1 (10th: +2) to their next attack or save.

system.description:
You master the art of Power attacks. All weapons with the ability to shatter bones and crack stone are treated as extensions of your fists and feet. Weapons that qualify for this stance are known as Raid Weapons. You gain the following benefits:

When you take the Ready action, you can make a weapon attack as part of that action. On a hit, the target is knocked Prone. Attempting to stand from being knocked prone in this way costs a Bonus action, in place of movement until the end of the affected creatures next turn.

Raid Weapons with the Heavy property ignore its Strength ability score requirement..

When you score a critical hit with a Raid Weapon, the target gains 1 rank of Bruised.

Beginning at 5th level when you make a weapon attack or a melee Taijutsu attack using a Raid Weapon, you can replace one attack with a Raiding Strike.

Raiding Strike. Make a weapon attack against a creature. On a hit, deal your [Weapon Damage] with pierce 4. If an interposing construct, structure creature would intercept this attack, double the Pierce value to 8.

Beginning at 10th level, when you deal damage with a Raiding Strike to an interposing construct, structure or creature, increase its damage by its Pierce value.

activities.label: Raiding Strike
activities.text: Pierce 8 against an interposing construct, structure or creature.

system.description:
You are a Sensory-Nin with the skills to track, analyze and intuit chakra, techniques and even strategies. You gain the following benefits:

Attacks from a hidden creature cannot surprise you.

Attacks from a hidden creature cannot be made at advantage vs you or allied creatures within 5 feet of you.

You gain the Sense Minor Chakra skill action.

Sense Minor Chakra. As a Bonus action, you can make a Perception check using either Constitution or Wisdom vs the Passive Chakra control (Chakra control bonus + 10) of all creatures within 15 feet of you. On a success, you gain the benefit of the Chakra Sensing special sense against them for the duration until they either have 0 chakra or they make and succeed their Suppress Chakra skill action.

Evocation Ability – Lock On. While wielding a Combat Scroll, when you succeed on a Sense Minor Chakra check against a creature, you can memorize their chakra signature for the next minute. Your Combat Scroll attacks against a creature whose chakra signature you’ve memorized ignore interposing constructs, structures and creatures, and ignores cover as these attacks curve around obstacles.
system.requirement: Have a Ninjutsu or Genjutsu with the Sensory keyword on your known list.

system.description:
You have learned to enter a highly defensive stance, becoming more guarded and focused on blocking and absorbing damage.

Your [Unarmed Damage] die becomes a d6.

While in this stance, you gain the Reinforced armor property if you weren’t already benefiting from it. Your Reinforced value is equal to your Taijutsu ability modifier.

If you are wearing armor with a Reinforced property, you increase the armored Reinforced value by +2.

DR granted by the Reinforced property cannot be reduced by hostile effects.

Beginning at 5th level, when you take damage, you can spend your reaction to perform Titan Guard.

Titan Guard. You raise your guard, granting yourself a +2 bonus to your AC and your Reinforced value. This bonus lasts until the beginning of your next turn.

Beginning at 10th level, when you successfully use Titan Guard, you can immediately take the Attack action against the triggering creature, adding your Reinforced value to your [Unarmed Damage], if they are within your reach.

You are skilled at fighting with two weapons in a flurry of swings, strikes and attacks. Weapons that qualify for this stance are known as Dancer Weapons. You gain the following benefits:

Attacks made with the Multiattack property add your ability modifier to the damage if it didn’t already.

When you make an opportunity attack, you can attack with both of your Dancer Weapons.

Once per turn, when you take the Dash action, you can make one weapon attack, and compare the result against the AC of every hostile creature you move within reach of, once as part of that movement. You do not add your ability modifier to the [Weapon Damage].

Beginning at 5th level, when you make a weapon attack or a melee Taijutsu attack using a Dancer Weapon, you can replace one attack with a Flutter Attack.

Flutter Attack. Make one weapon attack with each of your Dancer Weapons against a single creature. If both attacks hit, they must make a Dexterity saving throw vs your Taijutsu save DC. On a failure, they are Dazed.

Beginning at 10th level, When you make a Flutter Attack and both attacks hit, you can spend your reaction to take the Dash action. Creatures you hit as part of this dash action cannot make opportunity attacks against you.
system.requirement: Two weapons with the Light or Multiattack weapon property in each hand.

activities.label: Flutter Attack
activities.text: One attack with each Dancer Weapon; the save only if both hit.

system.description:
Genjutsu you cast strike the precise cluster of nerves in your opponent’s brain forcing them to experience exactly what you want. You gain the following benefits:

When you cast a Genjutsu that requires an attack roll and miss, you can spend your Bonus action to remake the attack roll with advantage. Once you use this effect, you cannot do so again until you spend a Bonus action recharging this feature.

When you score a critical hit with a Genjutsu attack, the affected creature cannot react to this attacks damage, and they lose their reaction until the beginning of their next turn.

Evocation Technique – Double Frequency. While wielding a Combat Scroll, when you cast a Genjutsu that requires an attack, you can spend your Bonus action to make one Combat Scroll attack against the same creature. If both the triggering Genjutsu and the Combat Scroll attacks hit, then the next time the affected creature makes a Saving throw, they must use their lowest saving throw bonus, in place of their listed bonus.
system.requirement: Have a Genjutsu that requires an attack roll on your known list.

system.description:
Genjutsu you cast don’t just affect the mind, they also leave behind effects on the real world. You gain the following benefits:

Genjutsu you cast that force Intelligence saves, can instead require a Strength save if you spend a Bonus action as part of its casting.

Genjutsu you cast that deal psychic damage to a creature forces them to take a d4 penalty to the next Strength or Dexterity saving throw they make.

Once per turn, when you deal psychic damage as a result of a Combat Scroll attack you make, the affected creature suffers a d4 penalty to their next attack roll, before the end of their next turn.

Evocation Ability – Psionic Payload. While wielding a Combat Scroll, when a creature under the effects of a Genjutsu you are concentrating on, makes an attack. You can roll a d6. On a roll of 1, they miss, regardless of their attack roll. Once they miss in this way, they cannot be affected by this stance again until you complete a rest.
system.requirement: Have a Genjutsu that forces a saving throw on your known list.

system.description:
You can make shots that others find difficult. Weapons that qualify for this stance are known as Bullseye Weapons. You gain the following benefits;

Your weapons long range increment becomes its base range. Attacks within this range increment are not made at disadvantage.

The first ranged weapon attack you make each turn using a Bullseye Weapon against a creature that is unaware of you or you are Hidden from gains a +1 bonus to its critical threat range, and Pierce 4.

When you are targeted with a ranged attack that you can see, you may as a reaction, make a ranged weapon attack vs the triggering creatures ranged attack result. If your result is higher than theirs, you divert their attack by selecting a different creature within 30 feet of them, making that creature the new target of the triggering creatures attack.

Beginning at 5th level, when you make a weapon attack or a ranged Taijutsu attack using a Bullseye Weapon, you can replace one attack with a Pinpoint shot.

Pinpoint Shot. Make a weapon attack against a creature. On a hit, deal your [Weapon Damage]. If the target is unaware of you, you are hidden from them, or they are at your furthest possible range to target them, maximize its weapon damage die.

Beginning at 10th level, when you divert an attack using this stance, you can make one additional ranged weapon attack targeting the new target of the triggering creatures attack. When you hit with a Pinpoint Shot against a creature that is unaware of you, they must make a Constitution saving throw against your Taijutsu Save DC or become Bruised.
system.requirement: Ranged, Ammunition or Thrown Weapon Group

activities.label: Pinpoint Shot
activities.text: The die is maximized only if the target is unaware of you, you're hidden from it, or it's at your furthest range.

system.description:
You have studied in the Iron Fist fighting style. A closed fist fighting style, designed to break bone and directly injure opponents:

Your [Unarmed Damage] die becomes a d6. If wearing Combat Bracers this instead becomes 1d8 if Strength is your Taijutsu ability score.

While in this stance, your unarmed attacks gain the Heavy weapon property, but ignore the Ability score requirement.

Beginning at 5th level, Once per turn, in place of one of your attacks granted by the Attack action, you can perform a Bone Breaking Strike.

Bone Breaking Strike. Make an unarmed attack, dealing your [Unarmed Damage] and forcing a Strength saving throw vs your Taijutsu save DC on a hit. On a failure, the damaged creature has their AC reduced by 1 and are Bruised until the beginning of your next turn.

Beginning at 10th level, Your [Unarmed Damage] is doubled when dealing damage to a structure or construct. When a creature fails their saving throw against Bone Breaking Strike, their AC is instead reduced by 2 for the duration.

activities.label: Bone Breaking Strike: AC penalty
activities.text: On a failed Strength save.

system.description:
You are skilled in the art of defense, protecting yourself and your nearby allies. Weapons that qualify for this stance are known as Stalwart Weapons. You gain the following benefits.

When you take the Dodge action on your turn, you also gain advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

When an allied creature within 5 feet of you would take damage from an attack, you can spend your reaction to interpose yourself. The attack now targets you instead. The allied creature cannot be targeted by the same creature until the end of the current turn.

When you interpose yourself and the attack misses you, you can make one opportunity attack against the attacking creature if they are within your reach.

Beginning at 5th level, when you make a weapon attack or a melee Taijutsu attack using a Stalwart Weapon, you can replace one attack with a Guardian Strike.

Guardian Strike. Make a weapon attack against a hostile creature within your reach. On a hit, deal your Weapon Damage. Until the start of your next turn, the first time that creature would deal damage to an allied creature within 5 feet of you, reduce that damage by your Weapon Damage die result.

Beginning at 10th level, when you interpose using this stance to intercept damage, double your weapons Blocking property value, ignoring normal limits. The triggering attack does not automatically hit as normal, and instead if they miss, if you make an opportunity attack against the triggering creature, you can add your Blocking property value to the damage dealt.

activities.label: Guardian Strike
activities.text: Until the start of your next turn, the first damage it deals to an ally within 5 ft of you is reduced by your Weapon Damage die result.

system.description:
You have learned how to fight with the precision and ferociousness of a serpent: You fight with your fingers held to a point as your stab into an opponent’s pressure points like needles during acupuncture.

Your [Unarmed Damage] die becomes a d6 and piercing.

Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an unarmed attack, they gain a -1 penalty to their next d20 roll before the end of their next turn.

Beginning at 5th level, Once per turn, in place of one of your attacks granted by the Attack action or when you make a melee Taijutsu attack, you can perform a Serpent Grasp.

Serpent Grasp. Make an unarmed attack against a creature within your reach. On a hit, deal your [Unarmed Damage] and attempt to Grapple them using only one hand. While you have a creature Grappled this way, you can use an attack granted by the Attack action to use the enemy you are grappling as a weapon, swinging them into others, with the Serpents Rattle attack.

Serpents Rattle. While you are grappling a creature as a result of Serpents Grasp, you can force them to make a Strength saving throw vs your Taijutsu save DC. On a failure, you swing them like the end of a snakes tail, making an unarmed attack targeting a different creature, striking them with the grappled creature, dealing your [Unarmed Damage] + 2d6 to both the grappled creature and the target of the attack.

Beginning at 10th level, while you have a creature grappled as a result of Serpents Grasp they always suffer a -2 penalty to their first d20 roll per turn. This does not stack with this stances -1 penalty.

activities.label: Serpent Grasp
activities.text: On a hit, grapple it with one hand.

activities.label: Serpents Rattle
activities.text: On a failure, swing it into another creature: both take the damage.

system.description:
You master the use of weapons with a long reach, capable to striking enemies at a slight distance from you. Weapons that qualify for this stance are known as Lance Weapons. You gain the following benefits;

When you take the Attack action, you can use a bonus action to make one additional melee weapon attack with the opposite end of your weapon. The damage die for this attack is one step lower than the weapon's normal damage die.

Other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they enter your reach.

When you make an opportunity attack with a Lance Weapon, you can choose to push the triggering creature 10 feet in any direction instead of dealing damage. This forced movement can trigger opportunity attacks from your allies and it also spends the affected creatures movement if they have any remaining.

Beginning at 5th level, when you make a weapon attack or a melee Taijutsu attack using a Lance Weapon, you can replace one attack with a Sweeping Attack.

Sweeping Attack. Make a weapon attack targeting all creatures in a cone originating from you with a length equal to your weapon's reach, vs the AC of all creatures in range, dealing [Weapon Damage] on a hit. You can move all affected creatures 5 feet away from you as part of this attack.

Beginning at 10th level, when you move a creature as a result of this stances abilities, you can force them to make a Strength saving throw vs your Taijutsu save DC. On a failure, you knock them Prone.

activities.label: Opposite end
activities.text: After taking the Attack action.

activities.label: Sweeping Attack
activities.text: One roll against every creature in a cone as long as your reach; move them 5 ft.

system.description:
You have learned to fight with chakra and fists in a combination of leaping kicks and lunging punches, hitting creatures who are far outside of your attacks range.

Your [Unarmed Damage] die becomes a d6.

Once per turn, when an unarmed or Taijutsu has its damage intercepted by a structure or construct, you bypass those structures and constructs dealing damage as normal to the original target.

Beginning at 5th level, Once per turn, when you deal Unarmed Damage to a creature, you can leap to a space you can see within 15 feet of you. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks and cannot be reacted to.

Beginning at 10th level, your unarmed and Taijutsu attack range increases by +10 feet. When you leap as part of the Level 5 ability and land within reach of a second creature, you can make one unarmed attack against them as part of the same movement.

When casting jutsu that bombards an area with their effects, you are able to modify their shapes slightly. You gain the following benefits:

Ninjutsu or Genjutsu you cast that affects an area with a duration of Instant, leaves behind a lingering effect, until the beginning of your next turn. Hostile creatures that enter the affected area for the first time on a turn, suffer the effects of your jutsu as if they only Succeeded.

Ninjutsu or Genjutsu you cast that affects an area that normally does not allow you to choose creatures to affect, allows you now select one creature to make immune to your jutsu’s effects.

Evocation Ability – Motion Wave. While wielding a Combat Scroll, Ninjutsu or Genjutsu you cast that affects an area that has a duration and normally cannot be moved, can be moved as an Action. A jutsu can only be moved once in this way per casting. Creatures in the newly affected area makes their save as if they were in the original affected area.
system.requirement: Have a Ninjutsu or Genjutsu who’s area of effect is in the shape of a Sphere, Cube, Cone, Cylinder or Line, on your known list.

system.description:
You have learned how to fight with the rapid-fire speed of a rabbit: You fight with your feet as you strike multiple times with light kicks.

Your [Unarmed Damage] die becomes a d6.

While in this stance, your movement speed increases by 10 feet.

Your movement does not provoke opportunity attacks from creatures you have dealt [Unarmed Damage] to this turn.

Beginning at 5th level, Once per turn, in place of one of your attacks granted by the Attack action or when you make a melee Taijutsu attack, you can perform a Bunny Roundhouse.

Bunny Roundhouse. Make an unarmed attack, comparing the result to all hostile creatures within your unarmed attacks range, dealing your [Unarmed Damage] to each if it would score a hit.

Beginning at 10th level, Once per turn, as a Bonus Action, you can select a space you can see within 20 feet of you, and leap towards it, ending your movement there. If you end this movement within 5 feet of an allied creature you can throw them into a space of their choice that you can see within 20 feet of you as they land safely.

activities.label: Bunny Roundhouse
activities.text: One roll against every hostile creature in your unarmed range.

system.description:
Unique. This Stance counts as a Taijutsu Stance when gaining it as a result of a Class feature or Feat, and while you are unarmed.

You have learned how to strike with ruthless efficiency while you bring about death.

Weapons that qualify for this stance are known as Assassin Weapons;

Your [Unarmed Damage] die becomes a d6 and slashing and counts as an Assassin Weapon for all effects and abilities of this stance. If wearing Iron Claws this instead becomes 1d8.

While hidden from a creature, weapon attacks and unarmed attacks you make against them pierce half of their DR.

The first unarmed or weapon attack you make against a creature you are hidden from grants you +1 Critical threat range for that attack.

Beginning at 5th level, Once per turn, in place of one of your attacks granted by the Attack action, you can perform an Assassination Strike.

Assassination Strike. Make an unarmed attack or weapon attack using your Assassin Weapon against a creature you are hidden from. This attack maximized the Assassin Weapons damage die. After a successful attack resolves you can spend your Bonus Action to disengage.

Beginning at 10th level, Once per turn, when you disengage as a result of using Assassination Strike, you can spend your Reaction to attempt to Hide again, provided cover or concealment is available.
system.requirement: Iron Claws, or a weapon with the Deadly or Hidden weapon property.

activities.label: Assassination Strike
activities.text: Against a creature you are hidden from.

system.description:
You refine your chakra flow, to allow for elemental kneading and casting, simultaneously. You gain the following benefits:

When you take elemental damage from a hostile effect, of a damage type that matches a nature affinity you have, you can spend your Reaction, gaining resistance to the triggering damage.

When you would take elemental damage, you can spend your reaction, or if you used this stances reaction to gain resistance, as part of that reaction, make a Chakra Control Check vs creature who damaged you Ninjutsu save DC. On a success, until the end of your next turn, attack and damage rolls made with your Combat scroll are made with advantage.

While concentrating on two or more Ninjutsu with a nature release keyword, you reduce each cost to maintain concentration by 1.

Evocation Technique – Elemental Discharge. While wielding a Combat Scroll, when you cast a jutsu with a nature release keyword, you can make a Combat Scroll attack against one creature other than one affected by the triggering jutsu, as part of the same action.
system.requirement: Have a Ninjutsu with a nature release keyword on your known list.

system.description:
You have learned to enter a powerful and intimidating fighting stance. You fight with one hand as a claw and the other as a fist to emulate the ferocity of a Lion or Lioness.

Your [Unarmed Damage] die becomes a d6.

You gain a +1 bonus to checks and saves to resist gaining ranks of Demoralize or Shaken.

In place of one of your attacks granted by the Attack action, you can attempt the Demoralize Skill-action, using your Unarmed attack bonus in place of Intimidation.

Beginning at 5th level, Once per turn, if you would use the Demoralize Skill-action as part of this stance, make an attack as normal, dealing damage on a successful hit, and treating your attack result as the result of your Demoralize Skill-action..

Beginning at 10th level, the threat of your strikes escalate beyond just your person. When you would use the Demoralize Skill-action as part of this stance, you can instead make a Roaring Strike.

Roaring Strike. Make an unarmed attack, dealing your [Unarmed Damage]. All hostile creatures within 15 feet of your becomes targets of the Demoralize Skill-action, using your attack result in place of Intimidation.

activities.label: Roaring Strike
activities.text: All hostile creatures within 15 ft become targets of Demoralize, using this attack's result.
